enrichment.problem: Jobs created by CronJobs didn't expose the exact scheduled execution time. Users relied on parsing the Job name, which changed from second‑precision to minute‑precision, breaking scripts and observability tools.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use CronJobs and any tooling that inspects Job objects for schedule information were affected by the previous lack of explicit timestamp.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the annotation `batch.kubernetes.io/cronjob-scheduled-timestamp` on Job objects. The controller sets this annotation to the scheduled start time of the CronJob run.
enrichment.impact: Consumers can now reliably get the intended run timestamp directly from the Job object, eliminating brittle name‑parsing, improving debugging, monitoring, and any automation that needs the schedule time.

apiChange.description: A CDIDevice field is included in the Device Plugin's `ContainerAllocateResponse`. This field maps to the CDIDevice field in the CRI protocol.
apiChange.author: elezar
apiChange.userFacingChange: A CDIDevice field is includes in the Device Plugin's `ContainerAllocateResponse`. This field maps to the CDIDevice field in the CRI protocol.

enrichment.problem: Device plugins could not include CDI device information in their ContainerAllocateResponse, so the CDI device IDs were not propagated to the CRI layer and ultimately to containers.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using device plugins that need to expose CDI devices; node kubelet and container runtimes that handle allocation responses.
enrichment.fix: A CDIDevice field is added to the Device Plugin API's ContainerAllocateResponse and is mapped to the corresponding CDIDevice field in the CRI protocol, allowing plugins to return CDI device specs.
enrichment.impact: Enables proper propagation of CDI device specifications from device plugins through the kubelet to the container runtime, allowing workloads to consume CDI-defined devices without custom hacks.

apiChange.description:
Added namespace access support to the CEL expressions of ValidatingAdmissionPolicy via a `namespaceObject`
variable with expressions.
apiChange.author: cici37
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Added namespace access support to the CEL expressions of ValidatingAdmissionPolicy via a `namespaceObject`
variable with expressions.

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy CEL expressions could not reference namespace information, limiting the ability to write policies that depend on namespace labels, annotations, or other metadata.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and developers writing ValidatingAdmissionPolicy objects that need to evaluate namespace metadata.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a `namespaceObject` variable available in CEL expressions for ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, allowing policies to read namespace fields directly within their expressions.
enrichment.impact: Policy authors can now create more expressive admission policies that enforce rules based on namespace attributes, improving security, compliance, and operational flexibility without requiring custom admission webhooks.

apiChange.description: Added `ServedVersions` field to `StorageVersion` API.
apiChange.author: Richabanker
apiChange.userFacingChange: Add ServedVersions field to StorageVersion API

enrichment.problem: The StorageVersion API only exposed the list of stored versions for a resource, but did not indicate which of those versions are actually being served by the API server, limiting clients’ ability to discover and interact with the correct version.
enrichment.affected: Components and controllers that rely on the StorageVersion API (e.g., API aggregation layer, version‑negotiation proxies, custom controllers) will see the new field and can adjust their logic accordingly.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `ServedVersions` field in the `StorageVersion` API object, allowing the API server to publish the set of versions that are actively served for each storage resource.
enrichment.impact: Clients, proxies, and operators can now programmatically determine the currently served API version, improving version negotiation, unknown‑version interoperability, and overall cluster stability when dealing with storage version upgrades.

apiChange.description: Promoted API groups `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` and `ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding` to `v1beta1`.
apiChange.author: alexzielenski

enrichment.problem: The ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding API groups were only available in a pre‑release version (e.g., v1alpha1), limiting their stability and preventing production use.
enrichment.affected: Users who need to define and enforce validating admission policies, and cluster administrators managing admission control configuration.
enrichment.fix: Promoted both API groups to the v1beta1 version, making them a supported, versioned API that can be used in production clusters.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators and developers can now rely on a stable, versioned admission‑policy API for validating workloads, enabling broader adoption and integration with tools that require a non‑alpha API version.

apiChange.description: In the API Priority and Fairness feature, priority levels that are exempt from limitation can now be given a nominal and a lendable concurrency and their dispatching borrows from the concurrency limits of the other priority levels.  For details see https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/1040-priority-and-fairness#dispatching .
apiChange.author: MikeSpreitzer

enrichment.problem: Exempt priority levels in the API Priority and Fairness feature could not be configured with nominal or lendable concurrency, preventing them from participating in concurrency borrowing and limiting their traffic shaping capabilities.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use the API Priority and Fairness feature and have exempt priority levels (e.g., system components) could not set concurrency limits, limiting traffic shaping and fairness.
enrichment.fix: Introduces support for nominal and lendable concurrency on exempt priority levels and enables their request dispatching to borrow from the concurrency limits of other priority levels.
enrichment.impact: Provides administrators finer control over API request handling for exempt priority levels, improving traffic distribution, preventing potential overload, and enhancing overall fairness of API services.

apiChange.description:
Changed how KMS v2 encryption at rest can generate data encryption keys.
When you enable the `KMSv2KDF` feature gate (off by default), KMS v2 uses a key derivation function to generate single use data encryption keys from a secret seed combined with some random data. This eliminates the need for a counter based nonce while avoiding nonce collision concerns associated with AES-GCM's 12 byte nonce.
apiChange.author: enj
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Changed how KMS v2 encryption at rest can generate data encryption keys.
When you enable the `KMSv2KDF` feature gate (off by default), KMS v2 uses a key derivation function to generate single use data encryption keys from a secret seed combined with some random data.  This eliminates the need for a counter based nonce while avoiding nonce collision concerns associated with AES-GCM's 12 byte nonce.

issueContext.title: kmsv2: fix limitations caused by counter based nonce
issueContext.body: xref: https://hackmd.io/@enj/SyiXCABZn

enrichment.problem: KMS v2 encryption at rest used a counter‑based nonce for AES‑GCM, which could lead to nonce collisions and limited the ability to generate fresh data encryption keys safely.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use KMS v2 for encryption at rest, especially those that might hit nonce‑collision limits or require deterministic single‑use keys.
enrichment.fix: When the KMSv2KDF feature gate is enabled, KMS v2 now derives single‑use data encryption keys using a key‑derivation function (KDF) from a secret seed and random data, eliminating the counter‑based nonce.
enrichment.impact: Avoids potential nonce‑collision issues, making encryption‑at‑rest more reliable and secure for clusters using KMS v2. No operational changes are required unless the feature gate is enabled.

apiChange.description: Indexed Job pods now have the pod completion index set as a pod label.
apiChange.author: danielvegamyhre

enrichment.problem: Pods created by indexed Jobs did not expose their completion index via a pod label, making it difficult to select or filter pods for a specific index using label selectors.
enrichment.affected: Users of indexed Jobs (completionMode=Indexed) who need to identify pods by their completion index.
enrichment.fix: The Job controller now adds a label `batch.kubernetes.io/completion-index` (or similar) to each pod, setting its value to the pod's completion index.
enrichment.impact: Users can now query, monitor, and manage pods of indexed Jobs with standard label selectors, simplifying debugging, logging, and automated tooling that need to target a particular completion index.

apiChange.description: Added `IP mode` field to loadbalancer status ingress.
apiChange.author: RyanAoh
apiChange.userFacingChange: Add IP mode field to loadbalancer status ingress

enrichment.problem: LoadBalancer service status did not expose the IP mode (e.g., IPv4, IPv6, or dual‑stack), making it difficult for users and controllers to determine how the allocated address should be interpreted.
enrichment.affected: Users of Service type LoadBalancer, cloud‑provider implementations, and any tooling that inspects Service status for IP information.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `ipMode` field in the `LoadBalancerIngress` status of a Service. The API now returns the IP mode alongside the IP address, allowing callers to identify the address family or dual‑stack mode.
enrichment.impact: Clients, cloud‑provider controllers, and debugging tools can now correctly handle LoadBalancer IPs, especially in dual‑stack environments, improving reliability and observability of service exposure.

apiChange.description: Added new `CRDValidationRatcheting` alpha feature. During a PATCH or UPDATE Validation Ratcheting discards errors thrown by unchanged portions of the resource from most OpenAPI schema validations.
apiChange.author: alexzielenski
apiChange.userFacingChange: Adds new CRDValidationRatcheting alpha feature. During a PATCH or UPDATE Validation Ratcheting discards errors thrown by unchanged portions of the resource from most OpenAPI schema validations.

enrichment.problem: When patching or updating CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs), new OpenAPI schema validations could reject the request because they flag errors in fields that have not changed. This forced users to modify untouched fields to satisfy the new schema, making incremental updates cumbersome and error‑prone.
enrichment.affected: Users and operators who manage Custom Resources via PATCH or UPDATE calls, especially during CRD version upgrades or schema tightening.
enrichment.fix: Introduce the alpha feature `CRDValidationRatcheting`. During PATCH or UPDATE operations, validation ratcheting discards errors that originate from portions of the resource that were not modified, allowing most OpenAPI schema validations to ignore unchanged fields.
enrichment.impact: Operators can upgrade CRDs and their instances more safely and with less manual effort. Updates no longer fail due to legacy data in unchanged fields, reducing downtime and simplifying migration to stricter schemas.

apiChange.description: Added a new `namespaceParamRef` field to `admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1.ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`.
apiChange.author: alexzielenski

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy could not reference namespace-scoped parameters, limiting the expressiveness of admission policies that need to depend on namespace information.
enrichment.affected: Users creating or consuming ValidatingAdmissionPolicy resources, especially those needing namespace‑aware parameter references.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `namespaceParamRef` field to `admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1.ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`, allowing policies to refer to namespace parameters.
enrichment.impact: Policy authors can now write more flexible and powerful validating admission policies that consider namespace context, improving security and configurability without requiring work‑arounds.

apiChange.description: StatefulSet pods now have the pod index set as a pod label `statefulset.kubernetes.io/pod-index`.
apiChange.author: danielvegamyhre

enrichment.problem: StatefulSet pods did not have a built-in label exposing their ordinal index, making it difficult for users and tools to identify or select pods based on their index.
enrichment.affected: Users of StatefulSets who need to reference a pod’s index—for example, operators, custom controllers, and monitoring tools.
enrichment.fix: The StatefulSet controller now adds the label `statefulset.kubernetes.io/pod-index` to each pod, containing the pod's zero‑based ordinal index.
enrichment.impact: Enables easier pod selection, monitoring, and automation that depend on the ordinal (e.g., log aggregation, custom controllers, debugging) without needing to parse pod names.

apiChange.description: Added `podReplacementPolicy` and terminating field to job api.
apiChange.author: kannon92
apiChange.userFacingChange: add podReplacementPolicy and terminating field to job api

enrichment.problem: Jobs did not have a way to specify how completed pods should be replaced or to indicate when a Job was in the process of terminating, limiting control over pod lifecycle for batch workloads.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster running Jobs (batch/v1) that need custom pod replacement or termination handling; mainly affects developers and operators of batch workloads.
enrichment.fix: Introduces two new fields to the Job API: `podReplacementPolicy`, which lets users define the replacement behavior for fully terminated pods, and a `terminating` field to signal that a Job is shutting down. These fields are added to the Job spec/status and processed by the Job controller.
enrichment.impact: Users can now configure automatic pod replacement and safely detect termination, improving reliability and flexibility of batch Job workloads, especially for use‑cases that require precise pod lifecycle management.

apiChange.description:
The `IPTablesOwnershipCleanup` feature (KEP-3178) is now GA; kubelet no longer
creates the `KUBE-MARK-DROP` chain (which has been unused for several releases)
or the `KUBE-MARK-MASQ` chain (which is now only created by kube-proxy).
apiChange.author: danwinship
apiChange.userFacingChange:
The IPTablesOwnershipCleanup feature (KEP-3178) is now GA; kubelet no longer
creates the KUBE-MARK-DROP chain (which has been unused for several releases)
or the KUBE-MARK-MASQ chain (which is now only created by kube-proxy).

enrichment.problem: The kubelet was still creating the KUBE-MARK-DROP iptables chain (unused for several releases) and the KUBE-MARK-MASQ chain, which should only be managed by kube-proxy. This left stale/duplicated chains on nodes, potentially causing confusion or conflicts with network policies.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kubelet that previously emitted the unused KUBE-MARK-DROP chain or duplicated KUBE-MARK-MASQ chain. Network plugins and administrators who inspect iptables rules are directly impacted.
enrichment.fix: The IPTablesOwnershipCleanup feature (KEP‑3178) is now GA. kubelet no longer creates either the KUBE-MARK-DROP chain or the KUBE-MARK-MASQ chain. The MASQ chain is now created exclusively by kube-proxy.
enrichment.impact: Nodes have cleaner iptables configurations, eliminating unnecessary chains and reducing the risk of chain conflicts. This simplifies troubleshooting and ensures that iptables ownership is correctly managed between kubelet and kube-proxy.

apiChange.description: Graduated `AdmissionWebhookMatchCondition` feature to beta.
apiChange.author: a-hilaly

enrichment.problem: Admission webhook configurations could only use match conditions while the feature was in alpha, requiring a feature gate and providing no stable API guarantees.
enrichment.affected: Users and administrators configuring admission webhooks that rely on match conditions.
enrichment.fix: Graduates the AdmissionWebhookMatchCondition feature to beta, making the feature generally available and providing a stable API contract without needing an alpha feature gate.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now reliably use match conditions in admission webhook rules, improving request filtering and simplifying webhook configuration with a supported, production‑ready feature.

* create pods with lengthy strings in PodSpec (ie. large object size)
* observe memory usage of scheduler process

enrichment.problem: Follower (non-leader) kube-scheduler instances were retaining full cache data, causing unexpectedly high memory usage even when they were in standby mode.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with multiple kube-scheduler replicas, particularly those using follower/standby scheduler processes, and workloads that create large Pod objects.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the `delayCacheUntilActive` option in `KubeSchedulerConfiguration`. When enabled, follower schedulers defer caching of scheduling objects until they become the active leader, reducing memory consumption at the cost of a slight delay when leadership changes.
enrichment.impact: Standby scheduler processes now use far less memory, which is especially important for clusters running multiple scheduler replicas or handling large Pod specs. The trade‑off is a marginal increase in scheduling latency during a leader election.

issueContext.title: undeprecate kubelet --provider-id flag
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Un-deperecate the `--provider-id` kubelet flag, as this option is typically set per-node similar to `--node-ip` (which is not deprecated).

Or more generally, consider not deprecating fields available in config that make sense to set per-node.

### Why is this needed?

I noticed this while trying to ensure KIND moves towards not setting any deprecated flags, this one is tricky because it's not a fixed value.
https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kind/pull/2764

For a lot of kubernetes users, kubeadm is used for bootstrapping, and kubeadm supports supplying additional kubelet flags when configuring each node, but the kubelet config is cluster-wide, created during setting up the first node and uploaded to a configmap then used for all nodes.

In the future kubeadm may have the ability to do per-node kubelet config, but that effort will probably be involved and isn't staffed at the moment.

_technically_ you could run kubeadm in phases and then modify the config, but this is more complex to implement.

It's possible this won't be necessary if kubeadm patches can be extended to kubelet which may be a smaller feature change for kubeadm, but personally I think being able to configure simple per-node strings with a flag override is desirable for implementing clusters, and we've had the flag for many years with no trouble ...

 https://github.com/kubernetes/kubeadm/issues/1682#issuecomment-1124027039


The actual deprecation seems to be due to a blanket deprecation on things possible to set in config, and not targeted at this flag in particular.

See discussion in https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C0BP8PW9G/p1652465646070179

enrichment.problem: The kubelet --provider-id flag was deprecated, preventing users from configuring a per-node provider ID via a simple flag override. This caused difficulties for kubeadm, kind, and other setups that need node‑specific identifiers, because the kubelet config is cluster‑wide and lacks per‑node granularity.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and tooling (e.g., kubeadm, KIND) that need to set a unique provider ID for each node were unable to use the flag after its deprecation.
enrichment.fix: The --provider-id flag is re‑enabled (un‑deprecated) in the kubelet, restoring its original functionality so administrators can set a provider ID per node using the flag.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can again specify per‑node provider IDs without complex work‑arounds or awaiting per‑node kubelet config support. This simplifies node provisioning, especially for kubeadm‑based clusters and KIND, and restores compatibility with existing tooling that relies on the flag.

Following up from this discussion - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116420#issuecomment-1500602135

There are different components that fall in the critical path for the k8s API today (apiserver (core), authn/authz webhooks, mutating/validating/conversion webhooks, etcd, extension apiservers - maybe more I'm missing). While some of those do, bunch of them don't seem to have metrics tracking request/error counts and latency metrics. Here's what I found so far (will update as we learn more):

- [Authentication webhook](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ad18954259eae3db51bac2274ed4ca7304b923c4/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/filters/authentication.go#L47)

- [Authorization webhook](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ad18954259eae3db51bac2274ed4ca7304b923c4/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/filters/authorization.go#L45)
  - [x] request/error counts ([#117211](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117211))
  - [x] request latencies ([#117211](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117211))
- [Admission webhooks](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ad18954259eae3db51bac2274ed4ca7304b923c4/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/mutating/dispatcher.go#L186) (mutating/validating)
  - [x] request/error counts ([xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ad18954259eae3db51bac2274ed4ca7304b923c4/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/metrics/metrics.go#L201-L219))
  - [x] request latencies ([xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob

enrichment.problem: Cluster operators had no built‑in metrics for authorization webhook calls, making it impossible to track request counts, success/failure rates, or latency of these critical authz checks.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes cluster using the apiserver with external authorization webhooks; operators and monitoring systems that need authz metrics.
enrichment.fix: kube‑apiserver now exposes two new Prometheus metrics: `authorization_attempts_total` (a counter labeled by result) and `authorization_duration_seconds` (a histogram of request latency). These are emitted for every request to an external authorization webhook.
enrichment.impact: Provides visibility into the performance and health of authorization webhooks, enabling alerting, capacity planning, and faster debugging of authz‑related issues.

A V(2) log line that includes preemption details (preemptee and preemptor),

issueContext.title: dynamic resource allocation: use generated name for ResourceClaim from template
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Right now, the name is specified as `<pod name>-<claim source name inside pod spec>`. That's easy and deterministic, but may lead to conflicts with ResourceClaims that were created earlier, either automatically or manually.

Let's investigate the alternative: generate the name and let code which needs to know it search the API server or in a local cache via some label.


### Why is this needed?

Avoids conflicts.

enrichment.problem: When a ResourceClaim is created from a ResourceClaimTemplate, its name is deterministically set to `<pod>-<claim name>`. This can cause name collisions if a claim with the same name already exists (e.g., from a previous pod or a manually created claim), leading to creation failures for the pod.
enrichment.affected: Users running pods that reference ResourceClaimTemplates (dynamic resource allocation) and any controllers that create ResourceClaims on their behalf.
enrichment.fix: ResourceClaim names generated from a ResourceClaimTemplate now receive a random suffix while preserving the base `<pod>-<claim name>` prefix. The random suffix guarantees uniqueness, preventing name‑collision errors.
enrichment.impact: Pods that use dynamic resource allocation via ResourceClaimTemplates will no longer fail due to claim name conflicts. This improves reliability of workloads that depend on on‑the‑fly resource claims and reduces the need for users to manually manage claim names.

other.description: [KCCM] drop filtering nodes for the providerID when syncing load balancers, but have changes to the field trigger a re-sync of load balancers. enrichment.problem: The service controller filtered nodes by providerID when syncing load balancers. Cloud providers that do not set providerID on nodes were excluded, preventing load balancer provisioning for Services of type LoadBalancer.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters using cloud providers that do not populate node.providerID, especially those relying on Service type LoadBalancer.
enrichment.fix: The filtering by providerID is removed and any change to the providerID field now triggers a re‑sync of load balancers, ensuring load balancers are created even when nodes lack a providerID.
enrichment.impact: Enables load balancer creation for workloads on cloud providers without providerID support, restoring expected Service behavior and improving compatibility across providers.

other.description: Removed tracking annotation from validation and defaulting.
other.author: kannon92
other.userFacingChange: remove tracking annotation from validation and defaulting

enrichment.problem: The job tracking annotation was still present in the API validation and defaulting logic even after its deprecation, leading to unnecessary processing and potential validation errors for Jobs.
enrichment.affected: Users creating or managing Job resources that might have included the deprecated tracking annotation.
enrichment.fix: The deprecated tracking annotation has been removed from the Job validation and defaulting code paths, fully eliminating its handling in the API server.
enrichment.impact: Jobs no longer carry the stale tracking annotation, preventing validation failures and simplifying Job objects. This aligns the implementation with the deprecation KEP and reduces API server overhead.

enrichment.affected: Clusters upgrading to v1.28 that use a custom kube-scheduler configuration file based on the v1beta2 API version.
enrichment.fix: Migrate any existing kube-scheduler configuration files from `kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1beta2` to the supported `kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1` version.

other.description: Removed GA'ed feature gate `DelegateFSGroupToCSIDriver`.
other.author: carlory
other.userFacingChange: remove GAed feature gate DelegateFSGroupToCSIDriver

enrichment.problem: The GA feature gate `DelegateFSGroupToCSIDriver` was removed, so clusters that had this gate enabled can no longer rely on the delegated FSGroup handling provided to CSI drivers.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enabled the `DelegateFSGroupToCSIDriver` feature gate, and CSI drivers that relied on FSGroup delegation for volume permission handling.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate has been deleted from the codebase. The default behavior now follows the post‑GA implementation, and any code paths guarded by the gate have been cleaned up.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that explicitly enabled the gate must adjust their CSI drivers or volume security configuration, as FSGroup delegation will no longer be available. This may require updates to driver versions or pod security settings to maintain correct file ownership on volumes.

other.description: Removed GA'ed feature gate `DevicePlugins`.
other.author: carlory
other.userFacingChange: remove GAed feature gate DevicePlugins

enrichment.problem: The GA feature gate `DevicePlugins` was left in the code base even though the feature is always enabled, causing unnecessary configuration options and potential confusion for users who customize feature gates.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that include the `DevicePlugins` feature gate in custom kubelet or API server configuration files.
enrichment.fix: The `DevicePlugins` feature gate has been removed from the source code and documentation. Clusters no longer need to (and cannot) specify this flag in kubelet or API server configurations.
enrichment.impact: No functional behavior changes; device plugin support remains enabled. Users with custom kubelet or API server configs that explicitly set `DevicePlugins=true/false` must delete that entry to avoid validation errors.

other.description:
`kubeadm`: introduced a new feature gate `UpgradeAddonsBeforeControlPlane` to
fix a kube-proxy skew policy misalignment. Its default value is `false`. Upgrade
of the CoreDNS and kube-proxy addons will now trigger after all the control plane
instances have been upgraded, unless the fearure gate is set to true. This feature
gate will be removed in a future release.
other.author: pacoxu
other.userFacingChange: kubeadm: introduce a new feature gate UpgradeAddonsBeforeControlPlane to fix a kube-proxy skew policy misalignment. Its default value is `false`. Upgrade of the CoreDNS and kube-proxy addons will now trigger after all the control plane instances have been upgraded, unless the fearure gate is set to true. This feature gate will be removed in a future release.

enrichment.problem: During kubeadm upgrades the kube-proxy and CoreDNS addons could be upgraded before all control‑plane instances were upgraded, causing a skew in proxy policy configuration and potential traffic handling inconsistencies.
enrichment.affected: Clusters upgraded with kubeadm where the control‑plane and addon versions could become out of sync, particularly those using kube-proxy and CoreDNS addons.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the feature gate `UpgradeAddonsBeforeControlPlane`. With the gate disabled (default), kubeadm now upgrades CoreDNS and kube-proxy only after every control‑plane node has been upgraded. Setting the gate to true retains the old behavior. The gate will be removed in a future release.
enrichment.impact: Ensures consistent proxy policy and DNS behavior during upgrades, preventing temporary networking issues that could affect pod traffic. Users can control the upgrade order via the feature gate if needed.

other.description: Allowed container runtimes to use `ErrSignatureValidationFailed` as possible image pull failure.
other.author: saschagrunert
other.userFacingChange: Allow container runtimes to use `ErrSignatureValidationFailed` as possible image pull failure.

enrichment.problem: Container runtimes could not report a signature validation failure during image pulls, so kubelet could not differentiate these errors from other pull failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using CRI-compatible container runtimes that perform image signature verification; kubelet image pull logic is directly impacted.
enrichment.fix: The image pull error set now includes ErrSignatureValidationFailed, allowing runtimes to return this specific error code for signature validation problems.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability and handling of image signature verification issues, enabling better security monitoring and more precise retry or remediation logic in kubelet and related tooling.

### What would you like to be added?

### Why is this needed?

Currently, kube-proxy can be configured via both CLI flags and config file. and config file can override flags. In the future, all flags will be deprecated and use the config file instead. issueContext.title: helper function for unused storage feature in pkg/proxy/util
issueContext.body:
`pkg/proxy/util/utils.go` (which is supposed to be utility functions for kube-proxy) contains the function `NewFilteredDialContext` and associated struct `FilteredDialogOptions`, which are not used by kube-proxy and have nothing to do with service proxying. They were added in #91785 as part of a storage-related feature.

However this feature was apparently only ever implemented for two storage backends (scaleio and storageos), both of which have since been removed (#101685, #111620). So the current state is that you can set the associated [options in the kube-controller-manager config v1alpha1 API](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/91785/commits/f2e23afcf13fef805ad5341bd7a5625de5982d6c#diff-5ad0cddac612ee34ef81af71efaeae956cc08c468cf20ac2bf719aba980a73a6), and kcm constructs a `proxyutil.FilteredDialogOptions` which then gets passed around the volume controller, but there is no code that ever actually _uses_ that object.

I would like to get this code out of `pkg/proxy/util`, because it doesn't belong there. I was originally going to suggest moving it to `pkg/volume/util` or something, but given that it's essentially unused, maybe we should just revert #91785?

/sig storage

issueContext.title: Cleanup the Job controller exponential backoff delay
issueContext.body:
/sig apps

The code around Job controller exponential backoff delay has a lot of heritage. The purpose of this issue is to collect and discuss cleanup ideas. It was initiated by the backoff discussion under the KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3967#discussion_r1219690984.

Some fixes initiated by the discussion and small cleanups are already handled by the PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118470.

The source of the issue might be that the “backoff” delay is used in two different contexts:
- Value of the exponential backoff delay is computed based on the number of consecutive failures. It’s main purpose is to throttle pod creation rate when the pods fail: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L1415-L1419. 
- Value computed by the number of requeues in the queue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L1546-L1564

First, I suggest splitting the naming of these two different backoffs. Let’s use “api error backoff delay” and “pod failure backoff delay”. It would be good if the naming in the code reflected this difference.

Second, the “api error backoff delay” is used in non-obvious places:
- When handling a pod which is transitioning to failed phase: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4c40d749006a8895f6718f2b624a3dbe975988ab/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L321 (seems ok to drop)
- Where there is API conflict: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4c40d749006a8895f6718f2b624a3dbe975988ab/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L879

Also, I suggest having the following methods to requeue `syncJob` to make the intention clearer to the reader:
- `enqueueControllerImmediately(key)` - no delay
- `enqueueControllerDelayed(key)` - delayed by `max(1s, api error backoff)`
- `enqueueControllerDelayedByApiErrors(key)` - delayed by `max(1s, api error backoff)` [not sure we need it since the queue itself

enrichment.problem: Job controller only batched syncJob calls when the JobReadyPods feature gate was enabled, and its exponential backoff defaults were set to 10 seconds (default) and 6 minutes (max), causing unnecessarily long delays after API request failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Jobs that encounter API request failures or rely on the Job controller's sync loop. All workloads using Job resources are affected.
enrichment.fix: The change enables syncJob batching unconditionally, removing the dependency on the JobReadyPods feature gate, and lowers the default backoff to 1 second and the maximum backoff to 1 minute for API error retries.
enrichment.impact: Job controller recovers faster from transient API errors, reducing latency for Job processing and improving overall job throughput. Users see quicker job pod creation and less throttling during failure scenarios.

enrichment.problem: The pod garbage collector controller and other parts of kube-controller-manager were still using legacy log calls, making it harder to correlate log entries with specific controller contexts and to troubleshoot issues.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running the kube-controller-manager, especially when troubleshooting controller behavior or pod garbage collection.
enrichment.fix: Migrated the podgc controller and remaining log calls inside kube-controller-manager to the new contextual logging framework, completing the conversion of kube-controller-manager to use contextual logs.
enrichment.impact: Logs from kube-controller-manager are now enriched with context fields, improving observability, reducing debugging time, and providing consistent log formats across the control plane.

other.description: registered_metric_total, disabled_metric_total, hidden_metric_total & kubernetes_feature_enabled are promoted to `BETA` stability.
other.author: logicalhan

enrichment.problem: The metrics registered_metric_total, disabled_metric_total, hidden_metric_total, and kubernetes_feature_enabled were previously Alpha, providing no stability guarantee. Users of these metrics could experience breaking changes across releases.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using the promoted metrics for monitoring or alerting, including custom dashboards, Prometheus scrape configurations, and automated tooling that depends on metric stability.
enrichment.fix: Promoted the four metrics to BETA stability, indicating they have a stable semantics and will not change incompatibly without a deprecation cycle.
enrichment.impact: Consumers of Kubernetes metrics (e.g., monitoring, alerting, dashboards) can now rely on these metrics across minor releases, reducing churn and improving observability confidence.

other.description: Removed `KUBECTL_EXPLAIN_OPENAPIV3` which is already redundant.
other.author: ardaguclu
other.userFacingChange: Remove KUBECTL_EXPLAIN_OPENAPIV3 which is already redundant

enrichment.problem: The environment variable KUBECTL_EXPLAIN_OPENAPIV3 was defined but never used, making it redundant and potentially confusing for users.
enrichment.affected: kubectl users who might have set or referenced the KUBECTL_EXPLAIN_OPENAPIV3 environment variable.
enrichment.fix: The redundant KUBECTL_EXPLAIN_OPENAPIV3 environment variable has been removed from the kubectl codebase.
enrichment.impact: No functional change for users; the removal eliminates an unnecessary configuration option, simplifying kubectl usage and documentation.

other.description: Promoted the feature gate `ValidtaingAdmissionPolicy` to beta, and it is turned off by default.
other.author: alexzielenski
other.userFacingChange: Promoted the feature gate `ValidtaingAdmissionPolicy` to beta and it is turned off by default.

enrichment.problem: The ValidatingAdmissionPolicy feature was only available as an alpha gate and required manual enabling; its promotion to beta needed clear communication of its new stability level and default-off behavior.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use or plan to use admission control policies; administrators must explicitly enable the beta gate to activate the feature.
enrichment.fix: Promoted the feature gate `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` to beta status and kept it disabled by default, allowing clusters to opt‑in to a more stable admission‑policy implementation without breaking existing workloads.
enrichment.impact: Provides a more stable and vetted admission‑policy mechanism for clusters that enable it, while preserving backward compatibility by not enabling it automatically. Users can now rely on a beta‑grade feature for policy‑driven request validation.

deprecation.description: CephFS volume plugin (`kubernetes.io/cephfs`) has been deprecated in this release and will be removed in a subsequent release. The alternative is to use the CephFS CSI driver (https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/) in your Kubernetes cluster.
deprecation.author: humblec
deprecation.userFacingChange:
ACTION REQUIRED:  
CephFS volume plugin ( `kubernetes.io/cephfs`) has been deprecated in this release and will be removed in a subsequent release. Alternative is to use CephFS CSI driver (https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/) in your Kubernetes Cluster.

enrichment.problem: The built‑in CephFS in‑tree volume plugin (kubernetes.io/cephfs) is deprecated and will be removed in a future Kubernetes release, leaving clusters that still use it without a supported driver.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that have CephFS in‑tree volumes defined (PV/PVC) and workloads (Pods, Deployments, StatefulSets, etc.) that mount those volumes.
enrichment.fix: Migrate any PersistentVolume or PersistentVolumeClaim that uses the kubernetes.io/cephfs provisioner to the external CephFS CSI driver (github.com/ceph/ceph-csi). Deploy the CSI driver in the cluster and update PV/PVC definitions to reference the CSI driver.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that continue to rely on the in‑tree CephFS plugin will lose volume functionality once the plugin is removed, causing Pods that need CephFS storage to fail to start. Proactive migration avoids downtime and data‑access disruptions.

deprecation.description:
Deprecated support for CSI migration of `Ceph RBD volumes`. Users who were relying on Kubernetes' ability
to migrate to an out-of-tree storage driver should complete that migration before the support for it is removed.
deprecation.author: carlory
deprecation.userFacingChange:
ACTION REQUIRED:
Deprecated support for CSI migration of Ceph RBD volumes.

Users who were relying on Kubernetes' ability to migrate to an out-of-tree storage driver should complete
that migration before the support for it is removed.

enrichment.problem: Support for CSI migration of Ceph RBD volumes is being deprecated, meaning clusters that rely on Kubernetes to automatically migrate in-tree Ceph RBD volumes to the external CSI driver will lose that capability in a future release.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have Ceph RBD PersistentVolumes and rely on the built‑in CSI migration feature to move to the out‑of‑tree Ceph CSI driver.
enrichment.fix: The migration support is removed from the code base. Users must manually complete migration of their Ceph RBD PersistentVolumes to the external Ceph CSI driver before the support is fully removed.
enrichment.impact: Clusters using the in-tree Ceph RBD driver with CSI migration enabled will no longer be able to perform automatic migration, potentially causing volume provisioning failures unless the migration is completed ahead of time.

deprecation.description:
RBD volume plugin (`kubernetes.io/rbd`) has been deprecated in this release
and will be removed in a subsequent release. Alternative is to use RBD CSI driver
(https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/) in your Kubernetes Cluster.
deprecation.author: humblec
deprecation.userFacingChange:
ACTION REQUIRED:
RBD volume plugin ( `kubernetes.io/rbd`) has been deprecated in this release and will be removed in a subsequent release. Alternative is to use RBD CSI driver (https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/) in your Kubernetes Cluster.

enrichment.problem: The in-tree RBD volume plugin (kubernetes.io/rbd) is deprecated and slated for removal, which will break clusters that still use this plugin for Ceph RBD storage.
enrichment.affected: Clusters and workloads that provision or mount PersistentVolumes using the kubernetes.io/rbd in‑tree plugin.
enrichment.fix: Migrate storage workloads to the external RBD CSI driver (https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi/) before the plugin is removed.
enrichment.impact: Ensures continued access to Ceph RBD volumes after the in-tree plugin is removed, preventing storage failures for affected workloads.

deprecation.description: The deprecated flag `--lock-object-namespace` and `--lock-object-name` have been removed from kube-scheduler. Please use `--leader-elect-resource-namespace` and `--leader-elect-resource-name` or ComponentConfig instead to configure those parameters.
deprecation.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: The deprecated leader election flags `--lock-object-namespace` and `--lock-object-name` were still present in kube-scheduler, causing potential confusion and requiring users to migrate to the new flags.
enrichment.affected: Any deployment of kube-scheduler that used the removed `--lock-object-namespace` or `--lock-object-name` flags.
enrichment.fix: Removed the deprecated flags from kube-scheduler. Users should now configure leader election via `--leader-elect-resource-namespace` and `--leader-elect-resource-name` flags or through ComponentConfig.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that still used the old flags will fail to start the scheduler until the flags are updated, so administrators need to adjust their startup arguments or config files.

securityFixes.title: Insufficient input sanitization on Windows nodes leads to privilege escalation
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they include Windows nodes.

securityFixes.title: Insufficient input sanitization on Windows nodes leads to privilege escalation
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they include Windows nodes.

other.description: Fixes ability to build 1.28 without network access
other.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: Building Kubernetes 1.28 from source required network access, causing failures in offline environments or CI pipelines that lack internet connectivity.
enrichment.affected: Users building Kubernetes from source, especially in CI/CD pipelines or air‑gapped environments where network access is unavailable.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the build process and dependencies so that the source can be compiled entirely offline, removing the need for external network calls during the build.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI systems can now build Kubernetes 1.28 without internet access, improving reproducibility, reducing build failures, and enabling builds in air-gapped or restricted environments.

apiChange.description:
Fixed a bug where CEL expressions in CRD validation rules would incorrectly compute a high estimated cost for functions that return strings, lists or maps.
  The incorrect cost was evident when the result of a function was used in subsequent operations.
apiChange.author: jpbetz

enrichment.problem: CEL expressions in CRD validation rules incorrectly calculated a high estimated cost for functions that return strings, lists, or maps, causing validation to fail or be overly restrictive when those function results were used in subsequent operations.
enrichment.affected: Users defining CustomResourceDefinitions with CEL validation rules that include functions returning strings, lists, or maps.
enrichment.fix: The cost estimation logic was corrected so that functions returning strings, lists, or maps are assigned the proper estimated cost, preventing false high-cost rejections during CRD validation.
enrichment.impact: CRD validation behavior is now accurate, eliminating spurious validation failures and improving performance for users leveraging CEL in their CRD schemas.

apiChange.description: Mark Job onPodConditions as optional in pod failure policy
apiChange.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: The Job spec required the onPodConditions field in pod failure policy, forcing users to provide it even when not needed, leading to unnecessary validation errors.
enrichment.affected: Users defining Job resources with podFailurePolicy; manifests that omitted onPodConditions previously failed validation.
enrichment.fix: The onPodConditions field is now marked optional in the Job pod failure policy schema, allowing it to be omitted.
enrichment.impact: Users can create or update Job resources without specifying onPodConditions, simplifying configuration and reducing validation friction for workloads that don't need this condition.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.8
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which may lack recent security patches, performance improvements, and language bug fixes.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are rebuilt with the newer Go compiler.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.20.8 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components benefit from the newer Go runtime, bringing upstream security fixes, bug resolutions, and potential performance enhancements without requiring changes from users.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix OpenAPI v3 not being cleaned up after deleting APIServices
bugOrRegression.author: tnqn

enrichment.problem: When an APIService was deleted, the associated OpenAPI v3 specification was not removed from the API server, leaving stale schema data in discovery endpoints.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that dynamically register and later delete APIServices (e.g., aggregated API servers) could see outdated OpenAPI v3 data.
enrichment.fix: The cleanup logic for OpenAPI v3 specifications was updated so that deleting an APIService also removes its OpenAPI v3 entries, ensuring the discovery data stays consistent.
enrichment.impact: Prevents stale or incorrect API definitions from being served, reduces unnecessary memory consumption in the apiserver, and ensures clients get accurate discovery information.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a 1.28 regression in scheduler: a pod with concurrent events could incorrectly get moved to the unschedulable queue where it could got stuck until the next periodic purging after 5 minutes if there was no other event for it.
bugOrRegression.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.28 the scheduler could incorrectly move a pod that has concurrent events into the unschedulable queue, causing the pod to remain stuck for up to 5 minutes until the next periodic purge if no further events occur.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that receives multiple events in quick succession (e.g., updates, node status changes) in clusters running Kubernetes 1.28 could become unschedulable for up to five minutes.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler logic was corrected so that concurrent events no longer cause a pod to be misplaced in the unschedulable queue, ensuring it stays in the normal scheduling flow and can be retried promptly.
enrichment.impact: Pods that previously could be delayed by minutes will now be scheduled without unnecessary waiting, improving reliability and reducing latency for workloads that experience rapid successive events.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a concurrent map access in TopologyCache's `HasPopulatedHints` method.
bugOrRegression.author: Miciah

enrichment.problem: A data race could occur due to concurrent map access in the TopologyCache.HasPopulatedHints method, potentially causing panics in the network path that uses topology-aware service hints.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enable the Service Topology feature (topology-aware hints) and run kube-proxy on nodes.
enrichment.fix: Added proper synchronization to protect the map access in TopologyCache.HasPopulatedHints, ensuring safe concurrent reads/writes.
enrichment.impact: Prevents crashes of kube-proxy (and related network components) when services use topology-aware hints, improving cluster stability and reliability under load.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a 1.26 regression scheduling bug by ensuring that preemption is skipped when a PreFilter plugin returns `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.26 a regression caused the scheduler to perform preemption even when a PreFilter plugin returned `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`, leading to unnecessary preemption attempts and potential scheduling failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters upgraded to 1.26 where pods rely on PreFilter plugins that may return `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`; affected workloads could experience scheduling delays or failures.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now skips the preemption phase when a PreFilter plugin returns `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`, ensuring that pods are not incorrectly preempted.
enrichment.impact: Restores correct scheduling behavior, prevents needless pod preemptions, and improves cluster stability for workloads using PreFilter plugins after upgrading to 1.26.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a 1.27 scheduling regression that PostFilter plugin may not function if previous PreFilter plugins return Skip
bugOrRegression.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.27 a regression caused the scheduler’s PostFilter plugin to be skipped when earlier PreFilter plugins returned a Skip result, breaking custom scheduling logic that relies on PostFilter execution.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the kube-scheduler with PreFilter and PostFilter plugins, especially those with custom scheduling plugins that depend on PostFilter execution.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler code was corrected so that PostFilter plugins are always invoked regardless of Skip returns from preceding PreFilter plugins, restoring normal plugin flow.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that pods are evaluated correctly by PostFilter‑based plugins, preventing unexpected scheduling failures for clusters that use such plugins and maintaining expected scheduling behavior.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a 1.28 regression around restarting init containers in the right order relative to normal containers
bugOrRegression.author: gjkim42

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.28 a regression caused init containers to be restarted out of order relative to regular containers, breaking the contract that init containers must finish before normal containers start.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that uses init containers, especially those that depend on init‑container side‑effects before the main containers run.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet logic was updated to enforce the correct restart sequence, ensuring init containers are always started (or restarted) before any regular containers in a pod.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on init containers for setup now behave correctly after node or kubelet restarts, preventing failures or inconsistent state caused by out‑of‑order container launches.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a regression in default 1.27 configurations in kube-apiserver: fixed the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint feature (beta in 1.27+) to successfully fetch discovery information from aggregated API servers that do not check `Accept` headers when serving the `/apis` endpoint
bugOrRegression.author: Jefftree

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.27 the default kube‑apiserver configuration regressed: the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint beta feature failed to retrieve discovery data from aggregated API servers that serve the `/apis` endpoint without validating the `Accept` header, causing discovery calls to error.
enrichment.affected: Users running Kubernetes 1.27 with the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint feature enabled and using aggregated API servers that omit `Accept` header validation.
enrichment.fix: The kube‑apiserver was updated to correctly handle discovery requests to aggregated API servers that do not enforce `Accept` header checks, restoring proper fetching of discovery information when the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint feature is enabled.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that rely on aggregated API servers for extended APIs (e.g., custom API extensions, aggregated admission controllers) can now successfully discover those APIs, preventing broken `kubectl`/client discovery and ensuring feature availability.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a 1.28 regression handling negative index json patches
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes 1.28 introduced a regression where JSON Patch operations that use negative indexes (e.g., -1 for the last element) were processed incorrectly, causing patch requests to fail.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or tool that uses JSON Patch with negative indexes to modify Kubernetes resources, such as operators, scripts, and kubectl.
enrichment.fix: The API machinery’s JSON Patch handling code was corrected to restore proper support for negative index values, ensuring patches are applied as expected.
enrichment.impact: Clients that rely on JSON Patch (including kubectl patch and custom controllers) can again modify array fields using negative indexes without errors, restoring automation and preventing failed updates.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a bug where images pinned by the container runtime can be garbage collected by kubelet.
bugOrRegression.author: ruiwen-zhao

enrichment.problem: The kubelet could mistakenly garbage collect container images that were pinned by the container runtime, leading to missing images and pod start failures.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running kubelet with a container runtime that pins images (e.g., containerd, CRI‑O). Pods that depend on those pinned images could be impacted.
enrichment.fix: The garbage‑collection logic in kubelet was updated to recognize and preserve images that the container runtime has marked as pinned, preventing their removal.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that pinned images remain available on nodes, preventing unexpected pod restarts or failures and improving the reliability of workloads that rely on image pinning.

bugOrRegression.description: Ignore context canceled from validate and mutate webhook
bugOrRegression.author: divyasri537

enrichment.problem: When a validation or mutation webhook returned a context.Canceled error, the API server treated it as a failure, causing the original API request to be rejected even though the client had cancelled or timed out.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes client request that triggers a validation or mutation admission webhook (e.g., pod, deployment creation) could be erroneously rejected if the webhook returned context.Canceled.
enrichment.fix: The API server now ignores context.Canceled errors from validate and mutate webhooks, allowing the original request to complete (or be aborted client‑side) without being marked as a webhook failure.
enrichment.impact: Prevents spurious API request failures for workloads that use admission webhooks, improving reliability and user experience, especially in high‑latency or client‑cancel scenarios.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix nil pointer when etcd member is already removed
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm crashes with a nil pointer panic when attempting to remove an etcd member that has already been removed from the cluster.
enrichment.affected: Users running kubeadm commands that manage etcd members (e.g., `kubeadm reset` or `kubeadm upgrade`) in clusters where the member may have already been removed.
enrichment.fix: Added a guard in kubeadm's etcd member removal logic to detect already‑removed members and skip the removal step, preventing the nil pointer dereference.
enrichment.impact: Prevents kubeadm from exiting unexpectedly during etcd member removal or cluster upgrades, ensuring cluster lifecycle operations complete successfully.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.10
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which could miss important security patches, bug fixes, and performance improvements provided by newer Go releases.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source or using CI systems that compile the project. Existing clusters run the same binaries; no functional changes to workloads.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.20.10, ensuring that all components are compiled with the latest supported Go toolchain.
enrichment.impact: Developers, CI pipelines, and downstream distributors get binaries that benefit from Go's security updates and performance enhancements. The change may require updating build environments to Go 1.20.10 but does not affect runtime behavior of clusters.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.9
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which could miss security fixes, performance improvements, and may cause build incompatibilities with newer toolchains.
enrichment.affected: Users who compile Kubernetes from source and CI pipelines that build Kubernetes images.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.20.9, ensuring all components are compiled with the latest supported Go release.
enrichment.impact: Developers, CI/CD systems, and anyone building Kubernetes from source will now use a newer, supported Go runtime, reducing build failures and keeping binaries up‑to‑date with Go security patches.

failingTest.description: E2e framework: retrying after intermittent apiserver failures was fixed in WaitForPodsResponding
failingTest.author: pohly

bugOrRegression.description: Adds an opt-in mitigation for http/2 DOS vulnerabilities for CVE-2023-44487 and CVE-2023-39325 for the API server when the client is unauthenticated. The mitigation may be enabled by setting the `UnauthenticatedHTTP2DOSMitigation` feature gate to `true` (it is disabled by default). An API server fronted by an L7 load balancer that already mitigates these http/2 attacks may choose not to enable the kube-apiserver mitigation to avoid disrupting load balancer → kube-apiserver connections if http/2 requests from multiple clients share the same backend connection. An API server on a private network may choose not to enable the kube-apiserver mitigation to prevent performance regressions for unauthenticated clients. Authenticated requests rely on the fix in golang.org/x/net v0.17.0 alone. https://issue.k8s.io/121197 tracks further mitigation of http/2 attacks by authenticated clients.
bugOrRegression.author: enj

enrichment.problem: Unauthenticated clients could exploit HTTP/2 protocol vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-44487, CVE-2023-39325) in kube-apiserver, potentially causing denial‑of‑service attacks.
enrichment.affected: Unauthenticated clients contacting the kube-apiserver, especially those behind L7 load balancers or on private networks, could experience service disruption.
enrichment.fix: Introduces an opt‑in feature gate `UnauthenticatedHTTP2DOSMitigation` that, when enabled, activates mitigation logic for unauthenticated HTTP/2 requests. Authenticated requests are already protected by the upstream Go net library. The mitigation is disabled by default to avoid compatibility or performance impacts.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now protect the API server against HTTP/2 based DoS attacks when needed, while still being able to disable the mitigation for environments where it may cause connection sharing issues or performance regressions.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix 1.28.0 regression where adding aggregated APIService objects could cause apiserver to panic and affect the health check
bugOrRegression.author: Jefftree

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes v1.28.0, adding aggregated APIService objects could trigger a panic in the kube-apiserver, causing the server to crash and breaking the health check endpoint.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that create or register aggregated APIService objects (e.g., extensions via the aggregation layer) experienced apiserver panics and failed health checks.
enrichment.fix: The regression was corrected so that the apiserver no longer panics when aggregated APIService resources are created, restoring normal operation of the health check.
enrichment.impact: Prevents sudden apiserver crashes and health‑check failures for clusters that use API aggregation, ensuring higher availability and stability of the control plane.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug in cronjob controller where already created jobs may be missing from the status.
bugOrRegression.author: andrewsykim

enrichment.problem: The cronjob controller could omit already created Job objects from the CronJob's status, causing the status to not reflect all active jobs.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that uses CronJob resources and depends on its status (e.g., controllers, CI pipelines, monitoring tools).
enrichment.fix: The controller logic was updated to correctly track and include all Jobs that have been created by a CronJob, ensuring the status fields (such as active jobs) are accurate.
enrichment.impact: Users get reliable CronJob status information, which is important for monitoring, debugging, and cleanup of jobs. Incorrect status could lead to confusion or stale job cleanup.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a 1.28.0 regression where kube-controller-manager can crash when StatefulSet with Parallel policy and PVC labels is scaled up.
bugOrRegression.author: aleksandra-malinowska

enrichment.problem: kube-controller-manager could crash when a StatefulSet using the Parallel pod management policy and PersistentVolumeClaims with labels is scaled up, a regression introduced in v1.28.0.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Kubernetes 1.28.0 with StatefulSets that have the Parallel pod management policy and PVCs that carry labels, when those StatefulSets are scaled up.
enrichment.fix: The controller‑manager code now correctly handles PVC label processing during StatefulSet scaling, preventing the panic/crash scenario.
enrichment.impact: Restores stability of the control plane for clusters that use StatefulSets with parallel scaling and labeled PVCs, avoiding controller downtime and potential workload disruption.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug where containers would not start on cgroupv2 systems where swap is disabled.
bugOrRegression.author: klueska

enrichment.problem: Containers failed to start on nodes using cgroup v2 when swap was disabled, causing pods to remain pending or crash-loop.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes nodes using cgroup v2 with swap disabled; any pods scheduled to those nodes could not start.
enrichment.fix: Implemented a fix in the kubelet to correctly handle cgroup v2 environments without swap, allowing containers to be created and started normally.
enrichment.impact: Nodes that run Linux with cgroup v2 and have swap disabled can now run workloads without manual work‑arounds, increasing compatibility and stability for modern distributions.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixed a regression in kube-proxy where it might refuse to start if given
  single-stack IPv6 configuration options on a node that has both IPv4 and
  IPv6 IPs.
bugOrRegression.author: danwinship

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy could fail to start on nodes that have both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses when it is configured with single-stack IPv6 options, causing a regression.
enrichment.affected: Nodes that have both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses (dual‑stack) and are configured with only IPv6 options for kube-proxy.
enrichment.fix: The regression was fixed so that kube-proxy correctly handles single‑stack IPv6 configuration on dual‑stack nodes and starts without error.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that service traffic continues to be proxied on dual‑stack nodes using IPv6‑only settings, preventing loss of network connectivity for affected workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed an issue to not drain all the pods in a namespace when an empty-selector i.e. "{}" is specified in a Pod Disruption Budget (PDB)
bugOrRegression.author: sairameshv

enrichment.problem: When a Pod Disruption Budget (PDB) is created with an empty selector "{}", it incorrectly matches all pods in the namespace, causing `kubectl drain` to evict every pod instead of none.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using a PDB with an empty selector; any pods in the affected namespace could be unintentionally evicted during a drain.
enrichment.fix: Updated the PDB matching logic so that an empty selector is treated as no selector and does not select any pods, preventing unintended mass evictions during drain operations.
enrichment.impact: Prevents accidental disruption of all workloads in a namespace, improving reliability and preventing unexpected downtime for users who define PDBs with empty selectors.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed attaching volumes after detach errors. Now volumes that failed to detach are not treated as attached, Kubernetes will make sure they are fully attached before they can be used by pods.
bugOrRegression.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: When a volume detach operation failed, the volume was still marked as attached. Subsequent attach attempts could treat the volume as already attached, leading to pods being unable to use the volume or experiencing attach loops.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use PersistentVolumes and encountered detach errors, e.g., Pods, StatefulSets, Deployments, and any controller that mounts volumes.
enrichment.fix: The attach logic now correctly distinguishes volumes that failed to detach, ensuring they are not considered attached. Kubernetes now verifies that a volume is fully attached before allowing pods to use it.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on persistent volumes will reliably get the volume attached after a prior detach failure, reducing pod start failures and improving storage reliability for workloads such as StatefulSets and Deployments.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed bug to surface events for the following metrics: apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reload_failures_total, apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reload_last_timestamp_seconds, apiserver_encryption_config_controller_automatic_reload_success_total
bugOrRegression.author: ritazh

enrichment.problem: Events were not being emitted for the apiserver encryption config controller metrics (automatic reload failures, last reload timestamp, and success counts), preventing operators from seeing reload status via events.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using apiserver encryption at rest with automatic reload enabled; operators relying on events/metrics for monitoring reload status.
enrichment.fix: The code now surfaces events for the three encryption‑config‑controller metrics, ensuring that successes, failures, and timestamps are visible as events.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability and debugging of encryption‑at‑rest automatic reloads in the API server, helping operators detect and respond to configuration reload issues.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a bug where Services using finalizers may hold onto ClusterIP and/or NodePort allocated resources for longer than expected if the finalizer is removed using the status subresource
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: Services that have a finalizer can retain their allocated ClusterIP and/or NodePort after the finalizer is removed using the status subresource, causing the IP/Port to remain occupied longer than necessary.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes Service objects that use finalizers, especially when the finalizer is cleared via the status subresource.
enrichment.fix: The service controller now correctly releases ClusterIP and NodePort resources when a finalizer is removed via the status subresource, ensuring proper cleanup of allocated networking resources.
enrichment.impact: Prevents leakage of ClusterIP and NodePort allocations, avoiding potential exhaustion of service IPs and ports in clusters that use finalizers, leading to more reliable service provisioning.

bugOrRegression.description:
Revised the logic for DaemonSet rolling update to exclude nodes if scheduling constraints are not met.
  This eliminates the problem of rolling updates to a DaemonSet getting stuck around tolerations.
bugOrRegression.author: mochizuki875

enrichment.problem: DaemonSet rolling updates could become stuck when nodes did not satisfy scheduling constraints such as tolerations, preventing the update from progressing.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using DaemonSets with tolerations or other scheduling constraints; nodes where those constraints are not satisfied.
enrichment.fix: The DaemonSet controller's rolling‑update logic was revised to skip nodes that cannot schedule the new pods because required tolerations or other constraints are not met, allowing the rollout to continue on eligible nodes.
enrichment.impact: DaemonSet updates no longer hang, improving reliability and reducing manual intervention for clusters that use tolerations or other placement constraints.

bugOrRegression.description: Sometimes, the scheduler incorrectly placed a pod in the "unschedulable" queue instead of the "backoff" queue. This happened when some plugin previously declared the pod as "unschedulable" and then in a later attempt encounters some other error. Scheduling of that pod then got delayed by up to five minutes, after which periodic flushing moved the pod back into the "active" queue.
bugOrRegression.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: When a pod was first marked as unschedulable by a scheduler plugin and later encountered a different error, the scheduler incorrectly re‑queued the pod in the "unschedulable" queue instead of the "backoff" queue. This caused the pod to be delayed for up to five minutes before being flushed back to the active queue.
enrichment.affected: All workloads whose pods are scheduled by kube-scheduler and that may be marked unschedulable by a plugin before encountering another scheduling error.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler’s queue handling logic was corrected so that pods that transition from an unschedulable state to encountering another error are placed in the backoff queue, ensuring they are retried after the appropriate backoff interval.
enrichment.impact: Pods are no longer subject to an unnecessary five‑minute scheduling delay, leading to faster pod startup and more predictable scheduling behavior for workloads that rely on scheduler plugins.

other.description: Fixes an issue where the vsphere cloud provider will not trust a certificate if:

enrichment.problem: The vSphere cloud provider failed to trust a TLS certificate under certain conditions, leading to connection failures with the vSphere API.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters using the vSphere cloud provider (on‑prem vSphere environments).
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the certificate handling logic in the vSphere cloud provider to correctly trust valid certificates, ensuring proper TLS verification.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that rely on the vSphere cloud provider can now communicate with vSphere services without TLS errors, restoring functionality for node provisioning, storage, and other cloud provider operations.

other.description: The issuer of the certificate is unknown (x509.UnknownAuthorityError)

enrichment.problem: TLS connections failed with x509.UnknownAuthorityError because the certificate issuer was not recognized, causing components to reject the connection.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes control-plane components and clients that validate TLS certificates when communicating with the API server or webhook services.
enrichment.fix: The certificate verification logic was updated to correctly include and trust the appropriate Certificate Authority, allowing connections with properly signed certificates to succeed.
enrichment.impact: Components that communicate over TLS (e.g., API server, kubelet, controller manager, kubectl) can now establish secure connections without spurious failures, improving cluster reliability and security.

other.description: The requested name does not match the set of authorized names (x509.HostnameError)

enrichment.problem: TLS handshake fails with x509.HostnameError because the hostname requested by the client does not match any of the DNS names or IPs listed in the server certificate’s SANs.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes component or client that validates the API server’s certificate using a hostname that is not present in the certificate’s authorized names (e.g., kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl).
enrichment.fix: The change updates the certificate validation logic and adds clearer error handling, ensuring that components use the proper server name (or include the correct SANs in the certificate) so the handshake succeeds.
enrichment.impact: Components that communicate over TLS (e.g., kubelet, kube-apiserver, kubectl, kube-proxy) can now establish secure connections without spurious hostname validation failures, reducing outages caused by mis‑configured names or certificates.

other.description: The error surfaced after attempting a connection contains one of the substrings: "certificate is not trusted" or "certificate signed by unknown authority"
other.author: MadhavJivrajani

enrichment.problem: Connections to cloud provider endpoints failed with generic errors when the TLS handshake encountered an untrusted or unknown authority certificate, making it difficult to diagnose and sometimes blocking functionality.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use cloud provider integrations with TLS endpoints presenting untrusted or unknown‑authority certificates (e.g., on‑prem clouds, custom endpoints).
enrichment.fix: Improved the certificate validation path to correctly detect and surface "certificate is not trusted" and "certificate signed by unknown authority" errors, providing clearer diagnostics and allowing expected handling of self‑signed or custom CA certificates.
enrichment.impact: Users interacting with cloud provider APIs using custom or self‑signed certificates can now see accurate error messages and avoid unexpected connection failures, improving reliability of cloud‑provider integrations.

other.description: Set the resolution for the job_controller_job_sync_duration_seconds metric from 4ms to 1min
other.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: The job_controller_job_sync_duration_seconds metric was emitted with a 4 ms resolution, resulting in extremely high cardinality and overly granular data that could strain storage and make dashboards noisy.
enrichment.affected: Users collecting the job_controller_job_sync_duration_seconds metric (e.g., via Prometheus) and any dashboards or alerts that rely on its fine‑grained latency data.
enrichment.fix: The metric's resolution was changed to 1 minute, aggregating observations into one‑minute buckets.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the number of time‑series and storage overhead for the metric, improving Prometheus performance and dashboard readability. Users lose sub‑second granularity for this metric.

securityFixes.title: Insufficient input sanitization in in-tree storage plugin leads to privilege escalation on Windows nodes
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods and persistent volumes on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they are using an in-tree storage plugin for Windows nodes.

apiChange.description: Retry NodeStageVolume calls if CSI node driver is not running
apiChange.author: rohitssingh

enrichment.problem: When a CSI node driver is not running on a node, kubelet's NodeStageVolume calls fail and are not retried, causing pod volume mount failures and preventing pods from starting.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use CSI volumes on nodes where the CSI driver was temporarily unavailable; cluster operators seeing repeated pod start failures due to volume staging errors.
