enrichment.fix: Add retry logic in kubelet for NodeStageVolume calls when the CSI node driver reports not running, allowing the operation to be re-attempted until the driver becomes ready.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of CSI volume provisioning and pod startup, reducing transient failures and downtime for workloads that depend on CSI storage.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.11
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go compiler version, which lacked recent security patches and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes clusters and users running the official binaries, as well as downstream distributors who build Kubernetes from source.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.20.11, recompiling all components with the newer compiler.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components gain the security, bug‑fixes, and performance enhancements present in Go 1.20.11, reducing the risk of compiler‑related vulnerabilities and ensuring compatibility with future Go releases.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix 121094 by re-introducing the readiness predicate for externalTrafficPolicy: Local services.
bugOrRegression.author: alexanderConstantinescu

enrichment.problem: The readiness predicate was removed for services with externalTrafficPolicy=Local, causing nodes without ready endpoints to be considered for external traffic, leading to dropped connections or misrouted traffic.
enrichment.affected: Users running services with externalTrafficPolicy=Local (e.g., LoadBalancer services) in cloud or on‑prem environments.
enrichment.fix: Re‑introduce the readiness predicate so that only nodes with ready pods are eligible for serving external traffic for Local services.
enrichment.impact: Ensures reliable traffic routing for LoadBalancer/NodePort services using externalTrafficPolicy=Local, preventing traffic from being sent to nodes that cannot serve it.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixed a regression in default configurations, which enabled PodDisruptionConditions by default, 
  that prevented the control plane's pod garbage collector from deleting pods that contained duplicated field keys (env. variables with repeated keys or container ports).
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced by defaulting the PodDisruptionConditions feature caused the pod garbage collector in the control plane to skip deleting pods that contain duplicated field keys, such as duplicate environment variable names or container ports.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running pods that inadvertently contain duplicate environment variable keys or container port definitions were unable to have those pods garbage‑collected, leading to leftover pods.
enrichment.fix: The regression was fixed by correcting the default configuration so that the pod garbage collector correctly handles pods with duplicated keys and can delete them as intended.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that orphaned or terminated pods with duplicate env vars or ports are properly garbage‑collected, preventing resource leakage and keeping the cluster clean and stable.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed the issue where pod with ordinal number lower than the rolling partitioning number was being deleted it was coming up with updated image.
bugOrRegression.author: adilGhaffarDev

enrichment.problem: StatefulSet controller mistakenly deleted pods whose ordinal was lower than the rollingPartition value during a rolling update, causing those pods to be recreated with the new image before they should have been updated.
enrichment.affected: Users running StatefulSets with a non‑zero rollingPartition. Pods with ordinals lower than the partition were being deleted and recreated with the new image.
enrichment.fix: Fixed the StatefulSet controller logic to honor the rollingPartition setting, preventing deletion of pods with ordinals below the partition number and ensuring they retain their existing image until their turn in the rollout.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unintended pod restarts and premature image upgrades in StatefulSet rollouts, reducing the risk of service disruption for workloads that use partitioned updates (e.g., canary or phased deployments).

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes calculating the requeue time in the cronjob controller, which results in properly handling failed/stuck jobs
bugOrRegression.author: soltysh

enrichment.problem: The cronjob controller miscalculated the requeue delay, causing failed or stuck jobs to be requeued at incorrect times and not handled properly.
enrichment.affected: Users running CronJob resources that experienced failed or stuck jobs were impacted, as those jobs could remain pending indefinitely or be retried at wrong intervals.
enrichment.fix: Corrected the calculation of the requeue time in the cronjob controller so that failed or stuck jobs are requeued and processed at the intended schedule.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of CronJob workloads by ensuring failed or stuck jobs are retried or cleaned up correctly, preventing indefinite job hangs and reducing manual intervention.

bugOrRegression.description: Service Controller: update load balancer hosts after node's ProviderID is updated
bugOrRegression.author: cezarygerard

enrichment.problem: When a node's ProviderID changed (e.g., after node replacement or migration), the Service controller did not update the hosts list in the associated cloud load balancer, leaving stale IPs and potentially breaking traffic to LoadBalancer services.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using Service of type LoadBalancer that rely on cloud provider load balancers; particularly when nodes are recreated or their ProviderID changes.
enrichment.fix: The Service controller now watches for ProviderID updates on nodes and triggers an update of the load balancer hosts for affected Service objects, ensuring the LB reflects the current set of node IPs.
enrichment.impact: LoadBalancer services continue to route traffic correctly after node ProviderID changes, preventing outages or misrouted traffic in clusters that use cloud provider load balancers.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.12
feature.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which could miss recent Go security patches, performance improvements, and language/compiler bug fixes.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components and any downstream binaries built from the source tree are affected, since they now run on code compiled with Go 1.20.12.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.20.12, updating the build toolchain across the project.
enrichment.impact: Provides a more secure and performant runtime for every component (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.), reduces the risk of Go‑related vulnerabilities and takes advantage of compiler optimizations.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix panic if there are more terminating pods than active pods
bugOrRegression.author: kannon92

enrichment.problem: The deployment controller could panic when the number of terminating pods became larger than the number of active pods, causing a crash of the kube‑controller‑manager.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using Deployments (or ReplicaSets) that experience rapid pod terminations, such as fast rollouts or scale‑down events, could see the controller crash.
enrichment.fix: Added defensive checks in the controller logic to handle cases where terminating pod count exceeds active pod count, preventing the panic and ensuring graceful handling.
enrichment.impact: Prevents controller‑manager crashes in edge‑case scaling scenarios, improving cluster stability and ensuring deployments continue to reconcile correctly.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix: statle smb mount issue when smb file share is deleted and then unmount
bugOrRegression.author: andyzhangx

enrichment.problem: When an SMB file share was deleted, the mount point could become stale and the subsequent unmount operation would fail, leaving the volume in an unusable state.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use SMB (SMB CSI or in-tree) volume mounts, particularly on Windows nodes, where the share may be deleted while still mounted.
enrichment.fix: Added handling to correctly clean up stale SMB mounts after the underlying share is removed, ensuring unmount succeeds and the volume is properly released.
enrichment.impact: Prevents pods that use SMB volumes from hanging or encountering mount errors after the backing share is deleted, improving reliability of SMB storage on clusters.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixed a regression since 1.27.0 in scheduler framework when running score plugins. 
  The `skippedScorePlugins` number might be greater than `enabledScorePlugins`, 
  so when initializing a slice the cap(len(skippedScorePlugins) - len(enabledScorePlugins)) is negative, 
  which is not allowed.
bugOrRegression.author: kerthcet

enrichment.problem: In the scheduler framework, the number of skippedScorePlugins could exceed enabledScorePlugins, causing a negative length when initializing a slice (cap(len(skippedScorePlugins) - len(enabledScorePlugins))), which is invalid and could crash the scheduler.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the default kube-scheduler or custom scheduler extensions that employ score plugins; pods could have remained unscheduled due to scheduler crashes.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the initialization logic to handle cases where skippedScorePlugins > enabledScorePlugins, ensuring the slice capacity is never negative and the scheduler can safely run score plugins.
enrichment.impact: Prevents scheduler panics and restores normal pod scheduling for clusters that upgraded from 1.27.0, ensuring workloads continue to be placed without interruption.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a kube-apiserver log volume regression bug in default 1.27 configurations (introduced in 1.26, activated by the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint feature enablement in 1.27)
bugOrRegression.author: ritazh

enrichment.problem: Enabling the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint feature in the default 1.27 configuration caused kube-apiserver to emit an excessive number of log messages, leading to a regression in log volume that could fill log storage and make debugging harder.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Kubernetes 1.27 with the default configuration where the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint feature gate is enabled; primarily affects kube-apiserver logs.
enrichment.fix: The regression is corrected by adjusting the kube-apiserver logging behavior for the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint path, restoring the expected log volume in the default 1.27 configuration.
enrichment.impact: Reduces unnecessary log churn and storage consumption, making log streams more manageable and preserving observability tooling performance for clusters running the default 1.27 configuration with the feature enabled.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a regression in kube-scheduler memory use in default 1.28 configurations by moving the SchedulerQueueingHints feature gate back to disabled by default.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: The kube-scheduler started using excessive memory in the default 1.28 configuration because the SchedulerQueueingHints feature gate was unintentionally enabled by default, leading to a regression in memory consumption.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the default kube-scheduler configuration in Kubernetes v1.28 experienced higher memory usage, potentially impacting large clusters with many pending pods.
enrichment.fix: The SchedulerQueueingHints feature gate is moved back to being disabled by default, restoring the previous memory usage behavior.
enrichment.impact: Prevents the scheduler from consuming abnormal memory, reducing the risk of OOM crashes and improving cluster stability for users running the default 1.28 scheduler configuration.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes an issue where StatefulSet might not restart a pod after eviction or node failure.
bugOrRegression.author: aleksandra-malinowska

enrichment.problem: StatefulSet controller could fail to restart a pod after it was evicted or after a node failure, leaving the StatefulSet without the expected pod replica.
enrichment.affected: Users running workloads managed by StatefulSet that experience pod eviction or node failures were at risk of missing pods and reduced application availability.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the StatefulSet controller logic in kube-controller-manager to ensure it recreates pods when eviction events or node failures are observed, guaranteeing the desired replica count is restored.
enrichment.impact: Stateful workloads regain their expected replica count automatically, improving reliability and reducing manual intervention after node issues or evictions.

bugOrRegression.description:
The scheduling queue didn't notice any extenders' failures, it could miss some cluster events,
  and it could end up Pods rejected by Extenders stuck in unschedulable pod pool in 5min in the worst-case scenario.
  Now, the scheduling queue notices extenders' failures and requeue Pods rejected by Extenders appropriately.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: The scheduler's scheduling queue failed to detect failures from scheduler extenders, causing missed cluster events and leaving pods rejected by extenders stuck in the unschedulable pod pool for up to five minutes.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using scheduler extenders could experience pods stuck unschedulable for minutes, impacting workloads that depend on timely pod placement.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now monitors extender responses for failures and properly requeues pods that were rejected, ensuring they are retried promptly.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on custom extenders are scheduled without unnecessary delays, improving reliability and reducing the time pods spend in an unschedulable state.

other.description: Bump distroless-iptables to 0.2.8 based on Go 1.20.11
other.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: The distroless-iptables image used in Kubernetes testing was outdated, potentially lacking recent bug fixes and Go runtime updates.
enrichment.affected: SIG Testing workloads that rely on the distroless-iptables image for CI/e2e testing.
enrichment.fix: Update the distroless-iptables dependency to version 0.2.8, which is built with Go 1.20.11.
enrichment.impact: Testing environments (e2e, integration tests) will run with a newer, more stable iptables image, reducing test flakiness and ensuring compatibility with recent Go and security patches.

other.description: Makefile and scripts now respect GOTOOLCHAIN and otherwise ensure ./.go-version is used
other.author: BenTheElder

enrichment.problem: The build system did not honor the GOTOOLCHAIN environment variable, leading to inconsistent Go toolchain versions being used. In the absence of GOTOOLCHAIN, builds fell back to whatever Go version was on the PATH instead of the version specified in ./.go-version, causing reproducibility issues for developers and CI pipelines.
enrichment.affected: Developers building Kubernetes from source, CI/CD pipelines, and the Release and Testing SIG processes that compile the code.
enrichment.fix: Updated the Makefile and related build scripts to first check GOTOOLCHAIN and use it if set. If GOTOOLCHAIN is not set, the scripts now explicitly read and enforce the Go version defined in the repository's ./.go-version file.
enrichment.impact: Ensures deterministic builds across developer workstations and CI environments, reducing build failures and version mismatches. Improves reliability of release testing and CI pipelines that depend on a specific Go toolchain.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.13
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which could lack recent security patches, bug fixes, and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kubelet, kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller‑manager, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are rebuilt with Go 1.20.13.
enrichment.fix: The release updates the build process to use Go 1.20.13, recompiling all Kubernetes components with the newer compiler and standard library.
enrichment.impact: Clusters benefit from Go’s upstream security updates, runtime bug fixes, and performance enhancements without any user‑visible changes. Future feature development will also be compatible with the newer Go version.

bugOrRegression.description: Allow deletion of pods that use raw block volumes on node reboot
bugOrRegression.author: gnufied

enrichment.problem: Pods that used raw block volumes could not be deleted when a node rebooted, causing them to remain stuck and potentially leak resources.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that mounts a raw block volume (CSI or in‑tree) and runs on a node that is rebooted. The issue prevented proper pod deletion.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now permits deletion of pods that are backed by raw block volumes during node restart, cleaning up the pod and associated volume resources correctly.
enrichment.impact: Users running workloads with raw block CSI volumes will no longer encounter orphaned pods after node reboots, improving node lifecycle reliability and preventing resource leakage.

bugOrRegression.description: Etcd: Update to version 3.5.10
bugOrRegression.author: mzaian

enrichment.problem: The cluster was running an older etcd version that may contain bugs or security issues and lacks recent improvements.
enrichment.affected: Control‑plane components that communicate with etcd (kube-apiserver, kube‑controller‑manager, kube‑scheduler) and any workloads relying on consistent cluster state.
enrichment.fix: Kubernetes control‑plane components are updated to use etcd version 3.5.10, which incorporates upstream bug fixes and security patches.
enrichment.impact: Improves stability, reliability, and security of the data store used by the API server and other control‑plane components, reducing risk of data corruption or outages.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix: Mount point may become local without calling NodePublishVolume after node rebooting.
bugOrRegression.author: cvvz

enrichment.problem: After a node reboot, the mount point for a CSI volume could become a local mount without the kubelet invoking NodePublishVolume, causing the volume to be incorrectly mounted or inaccessible to pods.
enrichment.affected: Pods using CSI-backed persistent volumes on nodes that have been rebooted; workloads with stateful storage requirements.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now ensures that NodePublishVolume is called for CSI volumes after a node reboot, re-establishing the correct mount point and preventing it from being treated as a local mount.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on persistent CSI volumes retain correct access after node reboots, avoiding data access errors or potential downtime for stateful workloads.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixed a regression since 1.24 in the scheduling framework when overriding MultiPoint plugins (e.g. default plugins).
  The incorrect loop logic might lead to a plugin being loaded multiple times, consequently preventing any Pod from being scheduled, which is unexpected.
bugOrRegression.author: caohe

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in v1.24 caused the scheduling framework's loop logic for overriding MultiPoint plugins (e.g., default plugins) to load a plugin multiple times, which could block the scheduler from placing any Pod.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that override or rely on MultiPoint scheduler plugins; all Pods would fail to be scheduled under the broken logic.
enrichment.fix: The loop logic was corrected so that each MultiPoint plugin is loaded only once when overridden, restoring normal scheduling behavior.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that clusters using custom or default MultiPoint plugins can schedule Pods again, preventing cluster-wide scheduling deadlocks.

other.description: Reverts the EventedPLEG feature (beta, but disabled by default) back to alpha for a known issue
other.author: pacoxu

enrichment.problem: Enabling the EventedPLEG feature (released as beta) caused a known issue that could affect node stability or pod lifecycle handling.
enrichment.affected: Users who enabled the EventedPLEG beta feature on their nodes; clusters where the buggy implementation could cause pod lifecycle problems.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate for EventedPLEG is reverted back to alpha, removing the problematic beta implementation and restoring the previous stable behavior.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that had explicitly enabled EventedPLEG will no longer see the issue, preserving node reliability. Users who relied on the beta functionality must continue using the alpha version until the issue is resolved.

feature.description: Add process_start_time_seconds to /metrics/slis endpoint of all components
feature.author: richabanker

enrichment.problem: Components did not expose their process start time, making it difficult for operators to track component uptime and calculate SLI/SLAs.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes control‑plane and node components (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, etc.) that expose the `/metrics/slis` endpoint.
enrichment.fix: Adds a new `process_start_time_seconds` metric to the `/metrics/slis` endpoint of every Kubernetes component, reporting the Unix timestamp when the process started.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now monitor component uptime directly via Prometheus, improve SLI calculations, and more easily detect restarts or unexpected downtime, enhancing overall cluster observability.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.21.7

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes components were built with an older Go compiler version, lacking recent language improvements, security patches, and performance enhancements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are rebuilt with the newer Go version.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes binaries are now compiled using Go 1.21.7, updating the toolchain for the entire codebase.
enrichment.impact: Provides upstream security fixes, compiler optimizations, and ensures compatibility with future Go releases, reducing potential build‑time issues for downstream distributors and developers.

feature.description: update setcap/debian-base to bookworm-v1.0.1

enrichment.problem: The previous setcap and debian-base images were outdated and did not include recent security patches and library updates.
enrichment.affected: CI/CD systems and developers who use the setcap/debian-base images for building Kubernetes binaries or related tooling.
enrichment.fix: The images were rebuilt using the Debian Bookworm v1.0.1 base, bringing the setcap tool and underlying OS packages up to date.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI pipelines that build or run Kubernetes components with these images now benefit from newer security updates and bug fixes without needing to modify their workflows.

feature.description: update distroless-iptables to v0.4.5
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: The previous distroless-iptables image version could contain known bugs or security vulnerabilities that affect components relying on it.
enrichment.affected: Components that embed the distroless-iptables image, primarily kube-proxy and any other networking pods using it.
enrichment.fix: Updated the distroless-iptables dependency to version v0.4.5, incorporating upstream fixes and security patches.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the risk of iptables‑related failures or security issues for networking components, improving overall cluster stability and security.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixes a race condition in the iptables mode of kube-proxy in 1.27 and later
  that could result in some updates getting lost (e.g., when a service gets a
  new endpoint, the rules for the new endpoint might not be added until
  much later).
bugOrRegression.author: hakman

enrichment.problem: A race condition in the iptables mode of kube-proxy (versions 1.27 and later) could cause updates to be lost, such as new endpoint rules not being added promptly when a service’s endpoints change.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy in iptables mode (default for many users) on Kubernetes 1.27+; specifically services whose endpoints are updated.
enrichment.fix: Implemented a synchronization fix in kube-proxy’s iptables implementation to ensure that endpoint updates are applied reliably and without being dropped.
enrichment.impact: Service traffic will be routed correctly after endpoint changes, preventing stale or missing rules that could interrupt or misdirect traffic to pods.

bugOrRegression.description: If a pvc has an empty storageClassName, persistentvolume controller won't try to assign a default StorageClass
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: When a PersistentVolumeClaim specified an empty storageClassName (""), the persistent volume controller treated it as a defined value and did not attempt to apply the default StorageClass, leaving the PVC unbound.
enrichment.affected: Users creating PVCs without specifying a storageClassName (or setting it to an empty string) and any workloads that depend on those PVCs.
enrichment.fix: The controller logic was updated to treat an empty storageClassName as unset, so it now falls back to the cluster's default StorageClass and attempts provisioning.
enrichment.impact: PVCs that omitted a storageClassName or set it to an empty string will now be bound automatically using the default StorageClass, preventing pod start‑up failures and reducing manual intervention.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: do not upload kubelet patch configuration into `kube-system/kubelet-config` ConfigMap
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: kubeadm incorrectly uploaded a kubelet patch configuration into the `kube-system/kubelet-config` ConfigMap, potentially overwriting the existing kubelet configuration.
enrichment.affected: Clusters initialized or joined with kubeadm that use a kubelet patch configuration; nodes could receive an incorrect kubelet config.
enrichment.fix: The kubeadm workflow has been updated to stop uploading the patch configuration into the `kube-system/kubelet-config` ConfigMap, preserving the original kubelet config.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unintended changes to kubelet settings on nodes created or joined with kubeadm, reducing risk of node misconfiguration and service disruption.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix a bug where the --rootfs global flag does not work with "kubeadm upgrade node" for control plane nodes.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: `kubeadm upgrade node` ignored or failed to apply the `--rootfs` global flag when upgrading control plane nodes, causing upgrade commands to operate on the wrong filesystem.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where administrators run `kubeadm upgrade node` on control‑plane nodes with the `--rootfs` flag, typically in environments using non‑standard root filesystems.
enrichment.fix: The kubeadm implementation now correctly propagates and respects the `--rootfs` flag during `kubeadm upgrade node` for control‑plane nodes.
enrichment.impact: Users can reliably upgrade control‑plane nodes that run with an alternate root filesystem (e.g., in containers or chroots) without upgrade failures, improving upgrade reliability in custom deployment scenarios.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.21.8

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go compiler, lacking the latest language/runtime fixes and security updates.
enrichment.affected: Developers and CI pipelines that compile Kubernetes from source, as well as downstream distributors that bundle the binaries.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to compile Kubernetes with Go version 1.21.8, incorporating the newer compiler, runtime, and standard library improvements.
enrichment.impact: Improves overall binary security and stability for users building from source or relying on downstream builds. May require downstream projects to align with Go 1.21.8 toolchain, but has no functional impact on runtime behavior.

feature.description: update distroless-iptables to v0.4.6
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: No specific issue was reported; the change updates the distroless-iptables dependency to a newer version.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run Kubernetes images built with the distroless-iptables library, primarily kube-proxy, will receive the updated binary.
enrichment.fix: The distroless-iptables library used in Kubernetes images is upgraded to version 0.4.6.
enrichment.impact: Kubernetes components that rely on the distroless-iptables binary (e.g., kube-proxy) will run with the latest iptables implementation, bringing potential bug fixes, security improvements, and better compatibility.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix error when trying to expand a volume that does not require node expansion
bugOrRegression.author: gnufied

enrichment.problem: Kubelet returned an error when a PersistentVolumeClaim was expanded for a volume that only required PVC-side expansion and did not need node-level expansion, causing the expansion to fail.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using CSI drivers where PVC expansion does not require node expansion; administrators trying to resize such volumes were blocked.
enrichment.fix: Updated the volume expansion workflow to detect when node expansion is not required and skip the node expansion step, eliminating the erroneous error.
enrichment.impact: Users can successfully expand storage volumes that only need PVC expansion without encountering errors, improving reliability of storage operations.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug that an init container with containerRestartPolicy with `Always` cannot update its state from terminated to non-terminated for the pod with restartPolicy with `Never` or `OnFailure`.
bugOrRegression.author: gjkim42

enrichment.problem: Init containers that have containerRestartPolicy set to Always could not transition their state from terminated back to non-terminated when the pod’s restartPolicy was set to Never or OnFailure, causing the pod to become stuck in a terminated state.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use init containers with containerRestartPolicy=Always together with pod restartPolicy=Never or OnFailure.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet logic handling containerRestartPolicy was corrected so that init containers with policy Always can properly update their state for pods with restartPolicy Never or OnFailure.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on init containers with an always‑restart policy now report correct status and can continue their lifecycle, preventing pods from being incorrectly marked terminated and improving workload reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed cleanup of Pod volume mounts when a file was used as a subpath.
bugOrRegression.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: When a pod used a file as a volume subPath, the kubelet failed to correctly clean up the associated volume mount after the pod was terminated, potentially leaving stale mounts on the node.
enrichment.affected: Pods that specify a file as a subPath in a volume mount, and the nodes running those pods.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet’s volume cleanup logic was updated to correctly handle file‑based subPath volumes, ensuring that the mount is removed when the pod is deleted.
enrichment.impact: Prevents accumulation of unused mount points on nodes, reducing the risk of resource leaks and improving node stability for workloads that use file subPath volumes.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed the disruption controller's PDB status synchronization to maintain all PDB conditions during an update.
bugOrRegression.author: dhenkel92

enrichment.problem: During an update, the disruption controller's PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) status synchronization dropped existing PDB conditions, leading to incomplete or inaccurate PDB status.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads that rely on PodDisruptionBudgets for safe evictions or upgrades.
enrichment.fix: The synchronization logic was corrected to retain and propagate all existing PDB conditions when updating the PDB status.
enrichment.impact: Clusters with PDBs will now see correct status conditions, preventing unintended pod disruptions and ensuring reliable disruption budgeting.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes an issue calculating total CPU usage reported for Windows nodes
bugOrRegression.author: marosset

enrichment.problem: Kubelet incorrectly calculated the total CPU usage for Windows nodes, leading to inaccurate CPU metrics.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with Windows nodes that rely on CPU usage metrics for scheduling, autoscaling, or monitoring.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the calculation logic in the kubelet to correctly aggregate CPU usage on Windows nodes.
enrichment.impact: Provides accurate CPU usage data for Windows nodes, improving scheduling decisions, autoscaling, and monitoring reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: Prevent watch cache starvation by moving its watch to separate RPC and add a SeparateCacheWatchRPC feature flag to disable this behavior
bugOrRegression.author: mengqiy

enrichment.problem: The shared watch RPC used by the apiserver watch cache could become starved under heavy load, leading to delayed or missed watch events for clients and controllers.
enrichment.affected: Any component that relies on the apiserver watch API (e.g., controllers, custom controllers, CLI `kubectl` watch) could experience delayed events during high watch load.
enrichment.fix: The watch is now sent over a dedicated RPC per watch request, eliminating contention. A new feature gate `SeparateCacheWatchRPC` is introduced to allow disabling this behavior if needed.
enrichment.impact: Improves the latency and reliability of watch streams, preventing controller drift and ensuring timely propagation of resource changes across the cluster.

bugOrRegression.description: Restore --verify-only function in code generation wrappers.
bugOrRegression.author: skitt

enrichment.problem: The `--verify-only` flag was missing or broken in the Kubernetes code generation wrapper tools, preventing developers from running validation of generated code without modifying files.
enrichment.affected: Developers using Kubernetes API code generation tools (e.g., client-gen, deepcopy-gen) and CI systems that invoke `--verify-only`.
enrichment.fix: The `--verify-only` functionality has been restored in the code generation wrappers, allowing the flag to be used again for verification runs.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI pipelines that rely on `--verify-only` can now validate generated API client code, improving automation and preventing accidental changes from being introduced.

bugOrRegression.description: Updates google.golang.org/protobuf to v1.33.0 to resolve CVE-2024-24786
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes bundled an outdated version of google.golang.org/protobuf (prior to v1.33.0) that is vulnerable to CVE-2024-24786, exposing the control plane and client binaries to potential security exploits.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries that embed protobuf (kube-apiserver, kube-controller‑manager, kube‑scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, and any extension components relying on the API machinery).
enrichment.fix: The protobuf dependency is upgraded to v1.33.0 across the codebase, eliminating the vulnerable code paths introduced by the previous version.
enrichment.impact: Removes a critical security vulnerability, protecting clusters from possible remote code execution or denial‑of‑service attacks that could affect any workload or component that uses the protobuf library.

other.description: Build etcd image v3.5.12
other.author: bzsuni

enrichment.problem: The previous etcd container image used by Kubernetes was outdated and may contain known bugs or security issues.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that run the built-in etcd image (e.g., kube-apiserver's etcd backend) are affected; they should use the updated image to receive the fixes.
enrichment.fix: A new etcd container image version 3.5.12 is built and made available for Kubernetes components that embed etcd.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that upgrade to the new image benefit from bug fixes and security patches in etcd, improving cluster stability and data integrity.

securityFixes.title: Bypassing mountable secrets policy imposed by the ServiceAccount admission plugin
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where users may be able to launch containers that bypass the mountable secrets policy enforced by the ServiceAccount admission plugin when using containers, init containers, and ephemeral containers with the envFrom field populated.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.21.9

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go compiler, which may contain known bugs, security vulnerabilities, and performance issues.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) and any clusters running them.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.21.9, bringing in the latest language and runtime fixes, security patches, and performance improvements.
enrichment.impact: Improves overall stability, security, and performance of the Kubernetes control plane and node components for all clusters. Users benefit from a more reliable runtime with no functional changes required.

feature.description: update debian-base/set-cap to bookworm-v1.0.2
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: The Debian base image used by the set-cap component was outdated, potentially containing old packages and security fixes.
enrichment.affected: Any CI/CD pipelines, builds, or workloads that use the debian-base/set-cap image.
enrichment.fix: The debian-base/set-cap image was updated to the newer Bookworm version 1.0.2, bringing in updated packages and patches.
enrichment.impact: Users building or running workloads that depend on the set-cap image will benefit from newer libraries, bug fixes, and security patches without changing their own configurations.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix pod restart after node reboot when NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature gate is enabled and SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod disabled
bugOrRegression.author: bertinatto

enrichment.problem: Pods failed to restart after a node reboot when the NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature gate was enabled while the SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod feature gate was disabled, causing workloads using ReadWriteOncePod volumes to remain down.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with NewVolumeManagerReconstruction enabled and SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod disabled; workloads using ReadWriteOncePod volumes on nodes that reboot.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the kubelet's volume manager reconstruction logic to correctly handle pod restart paths under the specified feature‑gate combination, ensuring pods are re‑started after a node reboot.
enrichment.impact: Restores expected pod availability after node reboots for clusters using the NewVolumeManagerReconstruction gate, preventing downtime of workloads that rely on ReadWriteOncePod volumes.

bugOrRegression.description: Golang.org/x/net is bumped to v0.23.0 to address CVE-2023-45288
bugOrRegression.author: MadhavJivrajani

enrichment.problem: A security vulnerability (CVE-2023-45288) existed in the golang.org/x/net library, which is imported by many core Kubernetes components, potentially allowing malicious network interactions.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components that depend on golang.org/x/net, including the API server, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, and internal libraries.
enrichment.fix: The Go dependency has been updated to golang.org/x/net v0.23.0, which contains the patches that remediate CVE-2023-45288.
enrichment.impact: Clusters are no longer exposed to the vulnerability, reducing the risk of network‑level attacks across all workloads that interact with the Kubernetes control plane or client tools.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a 1.27+ regression in watch stability by serving watch requests without a resourceVersion from the watch cache by default, as in <1.27 (disabling the change in #115096 by default). This mitigates the impact of an etcd watch bug (https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/17555). If the 1.27 change in #115096 to serve these requests from underlying storage is still desired despite the impact on watch stability, it can be re-enabled with a `WatchFromStorageWithoutResourceVersion` feature gate.
bugOrRegression.author: serathius

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes 1.27 introduced a regression that served watch requests without a resourceVersion directly from storage, causing watch instability and exposing an etcd watch bug.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or controller that relies on the watch API (e.g., Deployments, StatefulSets, custom controllers) experienced unstable watches after upgrading to 1.27.
enrichment.fix: Reverted the change (#115096) by default so watch requests are served from the watch cache without a resourceVersion, restoring pre‑1.27 behavior. The original behavior can be re‑enabled via the `WatchFromStorageWithoutResourceVersion` feature gate.
enrichment.impact: Restores reliable watch semantics for controllers and clients, preventing premature watch termination and reducing the impact of the etcd watch bug, leading to more stable cluster operation.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix panic in the command "kubeadm certs check-expiration" when "/etc/kubernetes/pki" exists but cannot be read.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: kubeadm panics (crashes) when running `kubeadm certs check-expiration` if the /etc/kubernetes/pki directory exists but is not readable due to permission issues.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators using kubeadm to check certificate expiration; the panic prevented the command from completing.
enrichment.fix: Added proper error handling for unreadable PKI directory, preventing the panic and returning a descriptive error instead of crashing.
enrichment.impact: Administrators can safely run the certificate expiration check without kubeadm crashing, improving reliability of cluster maintenance tasks.

bugOrRegression.description: NONE
bugOrRegression.author: ritazh

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: Not specified
enrichment.fix: Not specified
enrichment.impact: Not specified

bugOrRegression.description: OpenAPI V2 will no longer publish aggregated apiserver OpenAPI for group-versions not matching the APIService specified group version
bugOrRegression.author: Jefftree

enrichment.problem: The kube-apiserver was publishing OpenAPI v2 definitions for aggregated API servers for group‑versions that did not match the group version declared in the APIService resource, resulting in inaccurate API discovery documents.
enrichment.affected: Users and tools that query OpenAPI v2 from aggregated API servers, especially those that relied on mismatched group‑versions being advertised.
enrichment.fix: The apiserver now filters OpenAPI v2 output for aggregated API servers, publishing definitions only for group‑versions that exactly match the APIService's specified group version.
enrichment.impact: Consumers of OpenAPI v2 (e.g., client code generators, Swagger UI, documentation tools) receive correct API specifications, avoiding confusion and potential usage of non‑existent or unsupported resources.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed PersistentolumeLabel providing wrong topology labels to Azure Disk PersistentVolumes when the external Azure cloud provider is used.
bugOrRegression.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: When using the external Azure cloud provider, PersistentVolumeLabel generated incorrect topology labels for Azure Disk PersistentVolumes, leading to inaccurate node topology information.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using Azure Disk PersistentVolumes with the external Azure cloud provider, especially workloads relying on topology constraints or zone‑aware scheduling.
enrichment.fix: Corrected the PersistentVolumeLabel logic to supply the proper topology labels for Azure Disk PVs when the external Azure cloud provider is in use.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that topology‑aware scheduling, zone‑aware workloads, and other features that depend on correct topology labels work as intended, preventing mis‑scheduling of workloads on Azure Disk storage.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug that a pod may remain unscheduled if any PreFilter plugin returns nodes that do not exist.
bugOrRegression.author: chengjoey

enrichment.problem: When a PreFilter plugin returned node names that did not exist, the scheduler could fail to place the pod, leaving it in an unscheduled (Pending) state indefinitely.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using custom or built‑in PreFilter plugins that incorrectly returned nonexistent node names, causing pods to remain unscheduled.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now validates the node list returned by PreFilter plugins and discards any nodes that are not present in the cluster, ensuring the scheduling cycle can continue with valid nodes.
enrichment.impact: Pods that were previously stuck pending due to malformed PreFilter output will now be scheduled normally, improving reliability of custom scheduling plugins and overall cluster workload placement.

other.description: For apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric, we are renaming the label for etcd to be "storage_cluster_id" instead of "cluster" to to reduce conflict and be very specific.
other.author: dims

enrichment.problem: The apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric used the label name "cluster" for etcd, which could conflict with other metrics and was not specific enough.
enrichment.affected: Users and systems that scrape or query the apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric, particularly those relying on the "cluster" label, will need to adjust their queries.
enrichment.fix: Renamed the etcd label on the apiserver_storage_size_bytes metric from "cluster" to "storage_cluster_id" to avoid conflicts and make the label purpose clear.
enrichment.impact: Monitoring and alerting queries that relied on the old label need to be updated, but the change prevents metric name collisions and improves metric clarity for users of Kubernetes storage observability.

apiChange.description:
Improved scheduling performance when many nodes, and prefilter returns 1-2 nodes (e.g. daemonset)
  For developers of out-of-tree PostFilter plugins, note that the semantics of NodeToStatusMap are changing: A node with an absent value in the NodeToStatusMap should be interpreted as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status
apiChange.author: gabesaba

enrichment.problem: When clusters have a large number of nodes and a prefilter step narrows the candidate list to only 1‑2 nodes (common for DaemonSet pods), the scheduler experienced degraded performance due to inefficient handling of the small candidate set.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with many nodes where prefilter narrows candidates to 1‑2 nodes (e.g., DaemonSet pods) and developers of out‑of‑tree PostFilter scheduler plugins.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler code was optimized to handle the case where prefilter returns a tiny node set, reducing the amount of work performed during scheduling. Additionally, the interpretation of NodeToStatusMap in out‑of‑tree PostFilter plugins was clarified: any node missing from the map is now treated as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status.
enrichment.impact: Scheduling cycles complete faster in large clusters, especially for DaemonSet workloads, improving overall cluster responsiveness. Plugin developers get a well‑defined status contract, preventing ambiguous scheduling decisions.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.21.10
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries are now built using Go version 1.21.10 instead of the previous version.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components built from source (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, etc.)
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to compile the codebase with Go 1.21.10.
enrichment.impact: Enables incorporation of bug fixes, performance improvements, and security updates from the newer Go compiler, without changing runtime behavior for clusters.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.21.11
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version, which could miss upstream security patches, bug fixes, and performance improvements provided by newer Go releases.
enrichment.affected: All clusters running binaries built with the previous Go version, i.e., any Kubernetes deployment using official builds, are affected by the upgrade.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.21.11.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) now benefit from the latest Go compiler fixes and security updates, reducing risk of compiler‑related vulnerabilities and ensuring better compatibility with future Go tooling.

bugOrRegression.description: Emition of RecreatingFailedPod and RecreatingTerminatedPod events has been removed from stateful set lifecycle.
bugOrRegression.author: atiratree

enrichment.problem: StatefulSet controller was emitting RecreatingFailedPod and RecreatingTerminatedPod events, which were unnecessary or misleading for users and monitoring tools.
enrichment.affected: Users and monitoring systems that listened for RecreatingFailedPod or RecreatingTerminatedPod events on StatefulSets will no longer see those events.
enrichment.fix: The emission of the RecreatingFailedPod and RecreatingTerminatedPod events has been removed from the StatefulSet lifecycle handling.
enrichment.impact: Operators and tooling that relied on these specific events will stop receiving them, reducing noise and preventing potential confusion. No functional behavior of StatefulSets changes.

bugOrRegression.description: Improved scheduling latency when many gated pods
bugOrRegression.author: gabesaba

enrichment.problem: When a large number of pods have scheduling gates, the kube-scheduler experienced high latency, delaying pod scheduling.
enrichment.affected: Users running workloads with many pods that use scheduling gates; clusters with high pod churn could experience delayed scheduling without this improvement.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler code was optimized to handle many gated pods more efficiently, reducing the time spent processing them and improving overall scheduling latency.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that use scheduling gates will see faster pod scheduling, leading to more responsive workloads and better scalability for large numbers of gated pods.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a 1.28 regression printing pods with invalid initContainer status
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.28, kube-apiserver incorrectly printed pod objects that had an invalid initContainer status, leading to misleading pod status information in API responses and CLI output.
enrichment.affected: Any user or automation that reads pod objects (e.g., kubectl get pods) when pods contain initContainers with invalid status entries.
enrichment.fix: The apiserver printing logic was corrected to properly handle and omit invalid initContainer status entries, restoring accurate pod status representation.
enrichment.impact: Clients such as kubectl, dashboards, and custom tooling now receive correct pod status data, preventing confusion and potential troubleshooting errors for workloads that use initContainers.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-scheduler: fixes a 1.28.10 regression that can lead to a scheduler crash when processing pods with affinity that doesn't match a real/valid node
bugOrRegression.author: AxeZhan

enrichment.problem: Kube-scheduler could crash when it processed pods that specified node affinity rules that did not match any real or valid node, a regression introduced in v1.28.10.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running v1.28.10 with pods that define node affinity pointing to nonexistent nodes could experience scheduler crashes, affecting all workloads waiting to be scheduled.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler code was corrected to gracefully handle invalid or non‑matching node affinity specifications, preventing a panic and subsequent crash.
enrichment.impact: Restores stability of the scheduler, ensuring clusters continue to schedule pods even when malformed affinity rules are present, avoiding downtime and scheduling outages.

bugOrRegression.description: Reduce critical section in watchcache to fix kube-apiserver scalability under heavy load of list requests
bugOrRegression.author: wojtek-t

enrichment.problem: The watchcache held a large critical section, causing the kube-apiserver to become a bottleneck under heavy list request load, leading to high latency or request failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with high list/watch traffic; any component or workload that issues many list requests to the kube-apiserver.
enrichment.fix: The critical section in the watchcache implementation was reduced, decreasing lock contention and improving the API server's ability to handle many concurrent list operations.
enrichment.impact: API servers now scale better under list‑heavy workloads, reducing request latency and preventing possible outages for clients that rely on frequent list/watch operations.

enrichment.affected: Developers and CI pipelines that compile Kubernetes from source; any environment that builds Kubernetes binaries.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to compile Kubernetes with Go 1.22.5, bringing in upstream language security patches, performance improvements, and future‑compatible toolchains.
enrichment.impact: All components built from source will benefit from the newer Go runtime and compiler, reducing potential build‑time incompatibilities and inheriting Go security fixes. This change does not affect runtime behavior for existing clusters.

bugOrRegression.description: Add `/sys/devices/virtual/powercap` to default masked paths. It avoids the potential security risk that the ability to read these files may offer a power-based sidechannel attack against any workloads running on the same kernel.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: The default unmasked sysfs path `/sys/devices/virtual/powercap` allowed processes in containers to read powercap files, which could be exploited for power‑based side‑channel attacks against co‑located workloads on the same kernel.
enrichment.affected: All pods and containers running on nodes where the kubelet applies the default masked paths could previously read powercap files; the change protects these workloads from being observed by malicious containers.
enrichment.fix: The path `/sys/devices/virtual/powercap` is now added to the default list of masked paths, preventing containers from reading these files unless explicitly unmasked by the node admin.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the attack surface on nodes by eliminating a potential side‑channel vector, enhancing isolation between workloads without requiring user intervention.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fix a bug that Pods could stuck in the unschedulable pod pool 
  if they're rejected by PreEnqueue plugins that could change its result by a change in resources apart from Pods.
  DRA plugin is the only plugin that meets the criteria of the bug in in-tree, 
  and hence if you have `DynamicResourceAllocation` feature flag enabled, 
  your DRA Pods could be affected by this bug.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: Pods could become permanently stuck in the unschedulable pod pool when they were rejected by PreEnqueue plugins that later changed their result due to external resource changes. The DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation) plugin was the only in‑tree plugin that exhibited this behavior, so pods using the DynamicResourceAllocation feature flag could remain unschedulable indefinitely.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with the `DynamicResourceAllocation` feature gate enabled and running pods that use the DRA plugin could experience pods that never get scheduled.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler logic was corrected so that pods rejected by PreEnqueue plugins are re‑evaluated when relevant resource changes occur, preventing them from remaining in the unschedulable pod pool.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on the DynamicResourceAllocation feature will now be scheduled correctly instead of being stuck, improving reliability for workloads that depend on dynamic resource allocation.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix endpoints status out-of-sync when the pod state changes rapidly
bugOrRegression.author: tnqn

enrichment.problem: Endpoints objects could become out‑of‑sync with the actual pod state when pods transition quickly (e.g., rapid scaling or restarts), leading to stale IPs in Service endpoints.
enrichment.affected: Users running Services backed by Pods that scale or restart quickly (e.g., Deployments, StatefulSets, custom controllers).
enrichment.fix: The endpoints controller now correctly reconciles endpoint slices/status even when pod state changes occur in rapid succession, ensuring the endpoint list stays current.
enrichment.impact: Services reliably route traffic to live pods, preventing connection errors and service disruptions for workloads that experience fast pod churn.

bugOrRegression.description:
For statically provisioned PVs, if its volume source is CSI type or it has migrated annotation, when it's deleted, the PersisentVolume controller won't changes its phase to the Failed state. 
  With this patch, the external provisioner can remove the finalizer in next reconcile loop. Unfortunately if the provious existing pv has the Failed state, this patch won't take effort. It requires users to remove finalizer.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: When a statically provisioned PersistentVolume (PV) that uses a CSI driver or has the migrated annotation is deleted, the PersistentVolume controller fails to set its phase to Failed, leaving the PV's finalizer in place. This prevents the external provisioner from cleaning up the PV, and if the PV is already in Failed state the issue persists, requiring manual finalizer removal.
enrichment.affected: Users who create statically provisioned PersistentVolumes backed by CSI drivers or with the migrated annotation. The issue appears during PV deletion.
enrichment.fix: The patch updates the PersistentVolume controller logic to set the PV phase to Failed on deletion for CSI‑type or migrated static PVs, allowing the external provisioner to remove the finalizer in the next reconcile loop. Existing PVs already in Failed state are not auto‑fixed; users must manually delete the finalizer.
enrichment.impact: Ensures proper cleanup of statically provisioned CSI PVs, eliminating stuck finalizers and reducing manual intervention, improving reliability of storage lifecycle management.

bugOrRegression.description: NONE
bugOrRegression.author: cji

enrichment.problem: Not specified
enrichment.affected: Potentially Windows nodes and related node components
enrichment.fix: Not specified
enrichment.impact: Not specified

apiChange.description: Fixed a bug in the API server where empty collections of ValidatingAdmissionPolicies did not have an `items` field.
apiChange.author: xyz-li

enrichment.problem: When listing ValidatingAdmissionPolicy objects, the API server omitted the `items` field for empty collections, violating the expected list schema.
enrichment.affected: Users or controllers that query the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy API and expect a standard list response were affected; they could encounter parsing errors or missing data when the list was empty.
enrichment.fix: The API server now always includes an empty `items` array in the response, even when no ValidatingAdmissionPolicy objects exist.
enrichment.impact: Clients that list ValidatingAdmissionPolicy resources (e.g., kubectl, controllers, admission webhook configurations) can reliably parse the response without errors, improving API consistency and tooling reliability.

apiChange.description: Use omitempty for optional Job Pod Failure Policy fields
apiChange.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: Optional fields in a Job's podFailurePolicy were always serialized, causing empty fields to appear in API objects and potentially leading to confusion or validation issues.
enrichment.affected: Users creating or reading Job resources with a podFailurePolicy that leaves optional fields unset; client libraries that consume Job objects.
enrichment.fix: The Job podFailurePolicy struct fields are now marked with `omitempty` so that they are omitted from the JSON/YAML output when not set.
enrichment.impact: Job objects are cleaner and smaller, improving readability and avoiding unnecessary empty fields that could interfere with client processing or validation.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix the bug where PodIP field is temporarily removed for a terminal pod
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: When a pod reaches a terminal phase (Succeeded or Failed), its PodIP field is cleared prematurely, causing the PodIP to be temporarily missing from the pod's status.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that observes or processes the status of a pod after it has terminated (e.g., monitoring, logging, automation scripts).
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the logic that updates pod status so that the PodIP field is retained for terminal pods until the pod object is fully garbage‑collected.
enrichment.impact: Commands like `kubectl get pod -o wide`, monitoring tools, and scripts that rely on a pod's IP after completion will no longer see a missing IP, preventing errors and improving reliability of post‑completion workflows.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug in ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that caused policies which were using CRD parameters to fail to synchronize
bugOrRegression.author: alexzielenski

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy objects that referenced CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) parameters failed to synchronize, causing the policies to be ineffective.
enrichment.affected: Administrators and workloads that rely on ValidatingAdmissionPolicy referencing CRD parameters were unable to enforce the intended validation logic.
enrichment.fix: Fixed the synchronization logic so that ValidatingAdmissionPolicy objects correctly handle CRD parameters and sync without errors.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that use ValidatingAdmissionPolicy with CRD parameters can now enforce admission rules reliably, preventing unexpected policy failures.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a 1.27+ regression watching a single namespace via the deprecated /api/v1/watch/namespaces/$name endpoint where watch events were not delivered after the watch was established
bugOrRegression.author: xyz-li

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.27 and later, establishing a watch on a single namespace using the deprecated endpoint /api/v1/watch/namespaces/<name> would silently stop delivering events after the watch was set up, causing clients to miss updates.
enrichment.affected: Any client or controller that watches a single namespace via the deprecated /api/v1/watch/namespaces/<name> endpoint.
enrichment.fix: The kube-apiserver code was corrected so that watch events are properly streamed to clients after the watch is established, restoring the expected behavior of the deprecated endpoint.
enrichment.impact: Clients that depend on namespace‑scoped watches (e.g., custom controllers, operators, scripts) regain reliable event delivery, preventing stale state and potential mis‑behaviour in workloads that relied on those watches.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a potential crash serving CustomResourceDefinitions that combine an invalid schema and CEL validation rules.
bugOrRegression.author: cici37

enrichment.problem: The kube-apiserver could panic and crash when serving CustomResourceDefinitions that had both an invalid OpenAPI schema and CEL validation rules, leading to API unavailability.
enrichment.affected: Users defining CustomResourceDefinitions with invalid schemas and CEL validation rules; clusters could experience apiserver crashes when processing those CRDs.
enrichment.fix: Added defensive checks and improved validation handling in the apiserver so that CRDs with an invalid schema combined with CEL rules no longer cause a server crash.
enrichment.impact: Prevents a potential cluster-wide outage for clusters using such CRDs, ensuring stability and continuous API access.

bugOrRegression.description: Mount-utils: treat syscall.ENODEV as corrupted mount
bugOrRegression.author: dobsonj

enrichment.problem: Mount utilities did not treat ENODEV errors from mount syscalls as indicating a corrupted mount, leading to stale or inconsistent mount state on nodes.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running kubelet that perform volume mounts (e.g., CSI, hostPath) could see mount failures or stale mounts; pods that depend on those volumes are affected.
enrichment.fix: The mount‑utils code now interprets syscall.ENODEV as a corrupted mount and performs cleanup/retry logic accordingly.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of volume mounting on nodes, preventing pods from failing to start or encountering mount‑related errors.

bugOrRegression.description: StatefulSet autodelete will respect controlling owners on PVC claims as described in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/4375
bugOrRegression.author: mattcary

enrichment.problem: When a StatefulSet with the autodelete feature was removed, its PersistentVolumeClaims were deleted even if other resources were listed as controlling owners, risking unintended data loss.
enrichment.affected: Users who enable StatefulSet autodelete and have PVCs that are also owned by other resources (e.g., backup jobs, other controllers).
enrichment.fix: The StatefulSet controller now checks for controlling owners on PVCs before deleting them, ensuring PVCs with additional owners are retained.
enrichment.impact: Prevents accidental deletion of PVCs that are still needed by other workloads or backup processes, protecting data integrity for users relying on shared or externally managed volumes.

bugOrRegression.description: Stop using wmic on Windows to get uuid in the kubelet
bugOrRegression.author: marosset

enrichment.problem: The Windows kubelet relied on the `wmic` command to retrieve the machine UUID. On systems where `wmic` is unavailable, deprecated, or fails, the kubelet could not obtain a UUID, leading to node registration failures or start‑up errors.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run Windows worker nodes; any workloads scheduled onto those nodes may have been impacted by node registration failures.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet no longer invokes `wmic` on Windows. It now uses a native Windows API method to obtain the UUID, eliminating the external command dependency.
enrichment.impact: Windows nodes can now start and register reliably without requiring the `wmic` tool, reducing startup failures and improving overall cluster stability for Windows workloads.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.6
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which may miss recent security patches and language improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components built from source (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) are rebuilt with the newer Go version, but runtime behavior remains unchanged.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to compile all Kubernetes components using Go 1.22.6.
enrichment.impact: Clusters run binaries built with a newer, supported Go runtime, gaining security fixes, performance enhancements, and future compatibility without requiring any changes from users.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a scheduler preemption issue where the victim pod was not deleted due to incorrect status patching. This issue occurred when the preemptor and victim pods had different QoS classes in their status, causing the preemption to fail entirely.
bugOrRegression.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: When a high‑priority pod preempted a lower‑priority pod, the scheduler failed to delete the victim pod because it patched the pod status with the wrong QoS class. If the preemptor and victim had different QoS classes, the preemption operation aborted and the victim pod remained, preventing the new pod from being scheduled.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that triggers preemption, especially when the preemptor and victim pods belong to different QoS classes (e.g., burstable vs. guaranteed pods).
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now patches the victim pod’s status correctly irrespective of QoS class differences, ensuring the victim pod is deleted and preemption succeeds.
enrichment.impact: High‑priority workloads can again preempt lower‑priority pods as intended, restoring expected scheduling behavior and preventing scheduling dead‑locks for clusters that rely on QoS‑based preemption.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix race condition in kube-proxy initialization that could blackhole UDP traffic to service VIP.
bugOrRegression.author: wedaly

enrichment.problem: A race condition during kube-proxy initialization could cause UDP traffic destined for a Service virtual IP to be dropped, effectively blackholing the traffic.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy for UDP services; any workloads relying on UDP traffic through Service VIPs.
enrichment.fix: The update synchronizes the kube-proxy startup sequence to eliminate the race, ensuring UDP packets are correctly programmed into iptables/ipvs and delivered to the backend pods.
enrichment.impact: UDP‑based services (e.g., DNS, media streaming) will no longer experience intermittent traffic loss, improving reliability of Service networking for affected workloads.

bugOrRegression.description: Terminated Pods on a node will not be re-admitted on kubelet restart. This fixes the problem of Completed Pods awaiting for the finalizer marked as Failed after the kubelet restart.
bugOrRegression.author: SergeyKanzhelev

enrichment.problem: When the kubelet restarts, pods that had already terminated (e.g., Completed Jobs) were re‑admitted to the node and remained in a terminating state. Their finalizer was never cleared, so the pod was later reported as Failed, causing false‑negative status for completed workloads.
enrichment.affected: Pods that have already terminated on a node (e.g., Completed Jobs) when the kubelet is restarted.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now excludes terminated pods from being re‑admitted after a restart. It ensures that completed pods are not subject to the termination finalizer and are correctly marked as Completed (or removed), preventing them from being reported as Failed.
enrichment.impact: Operators and controllers see accurate pod statuses after a node‑level kubelet restart. Jobs, CronJobs, and other workload controllers no longer treat healthy completed pods as failures, reducing unnecessary retries and alert noise.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.7
feature.author: haitch

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes source was built with an outdated Go version, which could cause build failures, miss security updates, and limit compatibility with newer Go toolchain features.
enrichment.affected: Developers, CI pipelines, and any environment that builds Kubernetes from source. No runtime impact for existing clusters.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.22.7, bringing the codebase in line with the current supported Go release.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that developers and CI systems can successfully compile Kubernetes, benefits from Go security patches and performance improvements, and prevents future build breakages.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.22.8
feature.author: haitch

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes builds previously used an older Go version; updating the toolchain is required to keep up with upstream Go releases.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source, including CI systems and developers, as all binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, etc.) are recompiled with Go 1.22.8.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to use Go 1.22.8 for compiling all Kubernetes binaries.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that developers and CI pipelines building Kubernetes from source benefit from the latest Go compiler improvements, security fixes, and performance enhancements, and prevents future build failures due to outdated toolchain versions.

bugOrRegression.description: Ensure daemonset controller to count old unhealthy pods towards max unavailable budget
bugOrRegression.author: ncdc

enrichment.problem: During a DaemonSet rolling update, the controller ignored old pods that were already unhealthy when calculating the maxUnavailable budget, potentially allowing more pods to be unavailable than the specified limit.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running DaemonSets that rely on maxUnavailable for rolling updates could experience excessive downtime; the fix protects all such workloads.
enrichment.fix: The DaemonSet controller now includes old unhealthy pods in the maxUnavailable count, ensuring the budget is respected throughout the update.
enrichment.impact: Users performing DaemonSet updates with maxUnavailable constraints will see reliable adherence to availability guarantees, preventing unexpected service disruption.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix a bug on the endpoints controller that does not reconcile the Endpoint object after this is truncated (it gets more than 1000 endpoints addresses)
bugOrRegression.author: aojea

enrichment.problem: When a Service has more than 1000 endpoint addresses, the endpoints controller truncates the list but fails to reconcile the Endpoint object, leaving stale or incomplete endpoint data.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Services with >1000 endpoints (e.g., large headless services, stateful workloads) experienced stale endpoint information.
enrichment.fix: The endpoints controller now performs a reconciliation after truncating the address list, ensuring the Endpoint object reflects the truncated set.
enrichment.impact: Services with a large number of endpoints now get accurate Endpoint objects, restoring correct service routing and preventing connectivity issues for workloads that rely on those services.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix wrong member list reported when removing an etcd member
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: When a user removed an etcd member using kubeadm, the tool reported an outdated or incorrect list of etcd members, leading to confusion about the current cluster membership.
enrichment.affected: Clusters managed with kubeadm where etcd members are removed; administrators relying on the member list output.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now correctly updates and returns the current etcd member list after a removal operation, ensuring the reported membership reflects the actual state.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators get an accurate view of etcd membership, preventing mis‑steps in troubleshooting or further member management and improving overall cluster reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: when adding new control plane nodes with "kubeadm join", ensure that the etcd member addition is performed only if a given member URL does not already exist in the list of members. Similarly, on "kubeadm reset" only remove an etcd member if its ID exists.
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: When adding a new control‑plane node with `kubeadm join`, the command could attempt to add an etcd member that already existed, and `kubeadm reset` could try to remove a member whose ID was not present, leading to etcd membership errors and failed joins or resets.
enrichment.affected: Users who add control‑plane nodes with `kubeadm join` or reset clusters with `kubeadm reset`, especially after a failed or repeated join attempt.
enrichment.fix: The join workflow now checks the current etcd member list and only adds a member if its URL is not already present. Likewise, `kubeadm reset` now verifies the member ID before attempting removal.
enrichment.impact: Prevents duplicate etcd members and erroneous removal attempts, ensuring reliable control‑plane expansion and clean cluster teardown, reducing manual intervention and potential etcd inconsistencies.

other.description: Kubeadm: removed `socat` and `ebtables` from kubeadm preflight checks
other.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: kubeadm preflight checks required the presence of the socat and ebtables binaries, causing init/join to fail on systems where these packages are not installed or are no longer needed.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using kubeadm to initialize or join a cluster on a system that lacks socat or ebtables.
enrichment.fix: The preflight checks for socat and ebtables have been removed, so kubeadm no longer validates their existence before bootstrapping a cluster.
enrichment.impact: Users can bootstrap clusters with kubeadm without having to install unnecessary networking utilities, reducing setup friction and avoiding false‑positive failures, especially on newer distributions that use nftables instead of ebtables.
